issues.main_description_html:
Issue #52 — Ranking Freshness: Penalty Mechanism Decision

Status: Done (decision recorded, implementation shipped in PR #60)
Type: Architecture decision, no code change of its own
Depends on: none — blocks #53, #54, #56, #57, #58

Problem

ranking is a stored column on DirectoryPhotographer (src/models/directory_photographer.go:27), written only by RecomputeAndSaveRanking (src/action/v1/photographers/computeRanking.go), which fires from 16 write paths. A profile untouched for over a year performs no writes, so RecomputeAndSaveRanking never fires for it — putting a freshness penalty inside ComputeRanking itself would be dead code for exactly the profiles it's meant to penalize.

Decision

Option A — query-time SQL expression. The v2 search orders by a penalized expression instead of the raw ranking column:

ORDER BY GREATEST(ranking - CASE WHEN (updated_at IS NULL OR updated_at < DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 365 DAY)) THEN 20 ELSE 0 END, 0) DESC
  • The ranking column keeps its current meaning: the base score (tierBaseline + fieldBonus). It is written exactly as before.
  • The penalty is never persisted — it's derived at read time, so it self-heals the moment any write bumps updated_at.
  • No migration, no schema change, no cron job. The repo has no migration mechanism at all, so this also avoids introducing one.

Rejected alternatives

  • Option B (persisted effective_ranking column + daily job): MySQL forbids non-deterministic functions (NOW()) in generated columns, for both VIRTUAL and STORED. This collapses into Option C plus an extra column — not a distinct mechanism.
  • Option C (bake penalty into ComputeRanking + daily BackfillRanking cron): Destroys the base score — once penalty is baked into ranking, a decayed Agency profile can no longer be distinguished from a fresh Pro one, and restoring a score requires a recompute instead of it happening automatically. Also introduces up to 24h staleness and a new cron dependency.

On query cost

ranking has no index today (no index gorm tags on DirectoryPhotographer, only unique constraints on gothru_user_id/slug/email), so the existing ORDER BY ranking DESC, rating_avg DESC, id DESC is already an unindexed filesort. Option A introduces no ordering regression versus the pre-existing baseline. Indexability was tracked separately in #56.

Outcome

Implemented in PR #60 (src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers.go). See issue-54-v2-search-ordering-implementation.md for the implementation detail.

Parent: GoThruMedia/gothru-photographer-v2#17

Blocks every other task in this breakdown. Pick the mechanism before writing code.

Problem

ranking is a stored column (src/models/directory_photographer.go:27), written only by RecomputeAndSaveRanking (src/action/v1/photographers/computeRanking.go:103), which fires from 16 write paths.

A profile that has not been updated in over a year performs no writes — so RecomputeAndSaveRanking never fires for it. Putting the freshness penalty inside ComputeRanking therefore makes it dead code for exactly the profiles it is meant to penalise. The score would only decay for profiles that are actively being edited, which is backwards.

Options

A. Query-time SQL expression (recommended)

Order the v2 search by the penalised score instead of the raw column:

ORDER BY (ranking - CASE WHEN updated_at < NOW() - INTERVAL 1 YEAR THEN <penalty> ELSE 0 END) DESC

The ranking column keeps its current meaning and is still written exactly as today — it holds the base score (tierBaseline + fieldBonus, 0-79). The penalty is never persisted; it is derived at read time.

  • Self-healing: the penalty appears and disappears purely as a function of the clock, no job required.
  • Satisfies AC3 for free — any write that bumps updated_at immediately restores the full score on the next query.
  • No migration, no schema change, no new infrastructure.
  • Cost: the v2 keyset-pagination cursor must compare the same expression (see #54).

B. New persisted column effective_ranking + scheduled job

Correction: an earlier version of this issue proposed a generated column. That is not possible. MySQL forbids non-deterministic functions (NOW(), CURRENT_DATE) in generated column expressions — for both VIRTUAL and STORED, not just STORED. A freshness penalty cannot be expressed as a generated column at all.

So this option is really: a plain column, filled by a daily job that walks the table and recomputes base - penalty.

  • Indexable, so ORDER BY and the keyset WHERE can both use an index.
  • Cost: a migration, a cron job to own and monitor, a full-table write sweep every day, and up to 24h of staleness at the boundary.
  • This collapses into option C plus an extra column — it is not a separate mechanism.

C. Penalty inside ComputeRanking + daily cron calling BackfillRanking

Smallest code diff — the existing BackfillRanking endpoint already walks every photographer (src/action/v1/photographers/maintenance.go:105).

  • Cost: up to 24h staleness, a full-table sweep daily, new cron infrastructure.
  • Worse: the base score is destroyed. Once penalty is baked into ranking, you can no longer distinguish a decayed Agency from a fresh Pro, and restoring a score requires a recompute rather than just happening.
  • Also collides with #55 — see that issue.

Recommendation

Option A. No migration, no scheduled job, base score preserved, and AC3 falls out automatically. The only real work is threading the expression through the keyset cursor (#54).

On the "won't a CASE in ORDER BY be slow?" objection

ranking has no index today. There are no index gorm tags on DirectoryPhotographer and no migration files in the repo — only unique constraints on gothru_user_id, slug and email. So the current ORDER BY ranking DESC, rating_avg DESC, id DESC already performs a filesort.

Option A therefore introduces no ordering regression. And if index-backed ordering is wanted, a composite index on (ranking, rating_avg, id) can be added independently — it is orthogonal to the penalty mechanism.

Latency on this query is dominated by other things entirely (dead cross-DB fetch, cross-DB IN lists, three Preloads). Measured in #56.

Done when

  • Mechanism chosen and recorded in a comment on this issue.
  • If not Option A, the dependent tasks in this breakdown are re-scoped accordingly.

issues.display_title: Issue #53: Ranking freshness: product decision for stale-profile penalty
issues.main_description_html:
Issue #53 — Ranking Freshness: Penalty Magnitude and Curve Decision

Status: Done — product decision codified in the issue body, implementation matches exactly
Type: Product decision, no code change of its own
Depends on: #52 — blocks #54, #58

Problem

The acceptance criteria required a "ranking penalty / score decay" without specifying a number. ComputeRanking (src/action/v1/photographers/computeRanking.go) produces tierBaseline(subscription) + fieldBonus.

Real score range (corrected)

MaxFieldBonus = 19 exists but only 14 scorable items are reachable (9 profile fields + 5 collection flags), so the clamp never engages — it's dead code. The real, non-overlapping score bands are:

Tier Subscription values Range
Agency 5, 8 60–74
Pro 1, 6 40–54
Basic 2, 7 20–34
PAYG / Free anything else 0–14

Because the tier step (20) is larger than the max field bonus (14), there is a 5-point unreachable gap between every tier band (15–19, 35–39, 55–59) — tier always dominates profile completeness today.

Decision

  • Flat penalty, not graded: -20, applied once updated_at < NOW() - INTERVAL 365 DAY (or updated_at IS NULL).
  • Formula: effective_ranking = max(base_ranking - 20, 0).
  • Boundary: <, not <=. Exactly 365 days old is still fresh.
  • NULL handling: treated as stale — no profile is exempt from freshness scoring by never having a recorded timestamp.
  • Floor: clamp at 0. Negative effective scores are unnecessary since ordering is the only consumer.
  • Intent — soft demotion, not a tier wipeout: a stale paid profile may still outrank a fresh lower-tier profile. At -20:
    • Any stale profile always ranks below every fresh profile of its own tier (band width 14–20 > penalty headroom within-tier).
    • A stale full Agency (74 − 20 = 54) ties a fresh full Pro (54) exactly — rating_avg then id break the tie. This is intentional, not an off-by-one: -20 sits just under the threshold (≥21) that would make a stale full Agency drop below every fresh Pro.
  • No time-scaling: a profile stale for 366 days and one stale for several years receive the identical -20 penalty. The penalty does not continue to grow.
  • Base column untouched: ranking remains the persisted base score; freshness is an ordering concern applied at query time, not a rewrite of the stored score.

Resolution history

This issue was originally opened with the "question" label pending product input. During implementation the decision was recorded twice as a comment (initial reasoning, then a correction after a review caught the MaxFieldBonus dead-code / real-range error). The issue body was subsequently rewritten by the product owner to codify the final decision directly — the codified body matches the implemented behavior exactly, verified line-by-line against src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers.go.

Outcome

Implemented in PR #60 as the freshnessPenalty = 20 / freshnessWindowDays = 365 constants in src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers.go, tested in getPhotographers_test.go (boundary, NULL, clamp cases). See issue-54-v2-search-ordering-implementation.md and issue-58-tests.md.

Parent: GoThruMedia/gothru-photographer-v2#17
Depends on: #52

Product decision

Photographer ranking should use a flat freshness penalty when a profile has not been updated in over one year.

The freshness penalty is intended to be a soft demotion, not a full reset of ranking power. A stale paid profile may still outrank a fresh lower-tier profile if its subscription tier and profile completeness are strong enough.

Current base score model

ComputeRanking returns:

base ranking = tier baseline + field bonus

Tier baselines:

Tier Subscription values Baseline
Agency 5, 8 60
Pro 1, 6 40
Basic 2, 7 20
PAYG / Free anything else 0

Field bonus currently comes from 14 scorable items:

  • 9 profile fields
  • 5 collection flags

Although MaxFieldBonus = 19 exists, only 14 points are currently reachable. Therefore the real current score bands are:

Tier Fresh score range
Agency 60-74
Pro 40-54
Basic 20-34
PAYG / Free 0-14

Freshness penalty rule

Apply the following effective ranking rule at query time:

effective ranking = max(base ranking - freshness penalty, 0)

The freshness penalty is:

20 points

The penalty applies when:

updated_at IS NULL
OR updated_at < NOW() - INTERVAL 365 DAY

Boundary behavior:

  • Exactly 365 days old is still considered fresh.
  • More than 365 days old is stale.
  • updated_at IS NULL is stale.
  • Effective ranking must never be negative.

Expected stale score bands

With a flat -20 penalty and a floor at 0:

Tier Fresh score range Stale effective score range
Agency 60-74 40-54
Pro 40-54 20-34
Basic 20-34 0-14
PAYG / Free 0-14 0

Product rationale

This penalty is intentionally meaningful but bounded:

  • A stale profile should rank below fresh profiles from the same tier.
  • Freshness should influence ranking, but should not completely erase subscription tier value.
  • The penalty should not continue increasing over time.
  • A profile stale for 366 days and a profile stale for multiple years receive the same -20 penalty.
  • The base ranking column should remain unchanged; freshness is an ordering concern, not a persisted score rewrite.

Implementation reference

Per #52, the chosen mechanism is query-time scoring. The stored ranking column remains the base score.

Implementation should apply the same effective ranking expression consistently in:

  • v2 search ordering
  • v2 keyset pagination cursor comparison
  • any response field decision documented by #54

Done when

  • #54 implements query-time effective ranking with the flat -20 freshness penalty.
  • #58 verifies stale, fresh, exact 365-day boundary, NULL updated_at, clamp-to-zero, reset behavior, and pagination stability.

issues.display_title: Issue #54: Ranking freshness: apply penalty to v2 search ordering and fix keyset cursor
issues.main_description_html:
Issue #54 — Apply Penalty to v2 Search Ordering and Fix Keyset Cursor

Status: Done — shipped in PR #60
Type: Implementation
Depends on: #52, #53

Scope

Apply the freshness penalty (#52 mechanism, #53 magnitude) to /v2/photographers/users search ordering, and keep keyset pagination correct across the penalty boundary. v1's getPhotographers.go (used only by the sitemap, per code inspection of every frontend fetcher) was explicitly out of scope and left untouched.

The core risk: keyset pagination

The existing cursor compared the raw ranking column in the WHERE clause while the intended ORDER BY would use a penalized expression. If the two diverge, pagination skips or duplicates rows across page boundaries — this was the primary implementation risk called out by the issue.

Implementation (src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers.go)

A single SQL expression is shared between ORDER BY and the keyset WHERE, built from the same Go constants used for the in-memory computation, so the two cannot silently drift apart:

const freshnessPenalty = 20
const freshnessWindowDays = 365

var effectiveRankingExpr = fmt.Sprintf(
    "GREATEST(ranking - CASE WHEN (updated_at IS NULL OR updated_at < DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL %d DAY)) THEN %d ELSE 0 END, 0)",
    freshnessWindowDays, freshnessPenalty,
)

func effectiveRanking(ranking int, updatedAt *time.Time, now time.Time) int {
    stale := updatedAt == nil || updatedAt.Before(now.AddDate(0, 0, -freshnessWindowDays))
    if stale {
        ranking -= freshnessPenalty
    }
    if ranking < 0 {
        ranking = 0
    }
    return ranking
}
  • ORDER BY: effectiveRankingExpr + " DESC", rating_avg DESC, id DESC — tiebreakers unchanged.
  • Keyset WHERE: the same effectiveRankingExpr string is substituted into the existing three-way OR comparison (rank / rank+rating / rank+rating+id), so the comparison and the ordering are provably the same expression.
  • Cursor row: its own effective score is computed in Go via effectiveRanking(cursorPhotographer.Ranking, cursorPhotographer.UpdatedAt, now) before being bound as a query parameter — not read as a raw column — so the cursor and the ordered rows are penalized consistently.
  • now is captured once per request and threaded through both the cursor computation and the per-row response mapping, so every row in a single response is judged against the same instant (and the boundary is deterministically testable — see #58).

API response field decision

Ranking in the JSON response (PhotographerResponse.Ranking) now returns the effective (penalized) score, not the raw stored column. Rationale: the response ordering already reflects the penalty; returning the raw column would show two profiles at the same number in a different order with no visible reason. This is a meaning change on a public field — documented in the PR description, and the stored ranking column itself is untouched.

Known accepted limitation (raised in PR review)

Cursor staleness is judged by the app clock (now, captured at request start); page rows are judged by NOW() in SQL (DB clock). A row sitting exactly at the 365-day boundary at request time can land on different sides of the two clocks, opening a seconds-wide skip/duplicate window. Accepted as-is (documented inline in the code) — narrow, and only affects rows crossing the boundary at that exact instant.

Verification

  • go build ./..., go vet ./... clean.
  • No changes to src/action/v1/photographers/getPhotographers.go (sitemap path).
  • Pagination-across-boundary regression test — see issue-58-tests.md.

Parent: GoThruMedia/gothru-photographer-v2#17
Depends on: #52, #53

This is the bulk of the work. Apply the freshness penalty to the v2 photographer search and keep pagination correct.

Why v2 only

Checked every frontend consumer in gothru-photographer-v2:

Fetcher Endpoint Used by
getPhotographers v1/photographers/users only src/app/sitemap.ts:18 — enumerates slugs for the sitemap, ordering irrelevant
getPhotographersV2 v2/photographers/users src/components/directory-page.tsx:166,189,228, src/app/page.tsx:86

Every user-facing ranked list goes through v2. v1 ordering is out of scope.

Before closing: confirm v1/photographers/users is not consumed by another client (admin panel, mobile). If it is, this task grows to cover src/action/v1/photographers/getPhotographers.go:83.

The tricky part: keyset pagination

src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers.go:254-264 currently pages with a keyset cursor comparing the raw ranking column:

query = query.Where(
    "(ranking < ?) OR (ranking = ? AND (rating_avg < ? OR rating_avg IS NULL)) OR (ranking = ? AND rating_avg = ? AND id < ?)",
    cursorRanking,
    cursorRanking, cursorRating,
    cursorRanking, cursorRating, cursorPhotographer.ID,
)

...then orders by ranking DESC, rating_avg DESC, id DESC.

If the ORDER BY uses a penalised expression while the WHERE still compares raw ranking, pagination breaks — rows get skipped or duplicated across page boundaries. Both the cursor comparison and the ordering must use the same expression.

Note the cursor is derived from cursorPhotographer.Ranking (the stored value loaded from the cursor row), so the penalised value has to be computed for the cursor row too, not just for the rows being compared.

Issue #55 — Bump photographers.updated_at on Child-Table Writes (AC3)

Status: Done — shipped in PR #60
Type: Bug fix
Depends on: none directly, but required for #54's AC3 and #58's reset tests

Reported problem

Acceptance criterion 3 ("updating any profile section resets the decay penalty") keys off photographers.updated_at. Most profile sections live in child tables (portfolio, services, equipment, availability, sublocations), and writing them was assumed to never touch the parent row — 16 write-path call sites all call RecomputeAndSaveRanking afterward, but none of them write updated_at directly.

What investigation actually found

DirectoryPhotographer.UpdatedAt (*time.Time, field name UpdatedAt) is GORM's convention-recognized auto-update-time field (gorm/schema/field.go: any field literally named UpdatedAt with a Time data type gets AutoUpdateTime set with no explicit tag needed). RecomputeAndSaveRanking's existing config.GetConnPhotographers().Model(&p).Update("ranking", ranking) call already triggers that auto-bump on every invocation — confirmed empirically against GORM v1.31.1 by inspecting the exact SQL it emits via a sqlmock-backed probe: UPDATE photographersSETranking=?,updated_at=? WHERE id = ?.

So the real bug was the opposite of the one reported: updated_at was already being bumped on every RecomputeAndSaveRanking call — including from inside BackfillRanking's loop over the entire table (src/action/v1/photographers/maintenance.go). Every backfill run was silently wiping the freshness penalty for every photographer, not just leaving it unset for the 16 child-table write paths.

Fix (src/action/v1/photographers/computeRanking.go, maintenance.go)

Single choke point, not 16 call-site patches — every write path already funnels through RecomputeAndSaveRanking:

  • RecomputeAndSaveRanking(gothruUserId uint64) — unchanged public signature and behavior for the 14+ write-path callers. Internally calls recomputeAndSaveRanking(gothruUserId, preserveTimestamp=false), which uses GORM's .Update("ranking", ranking) — still bumps updated_at.
  • RecomputeAndSaveRankingPreserveTimestamp(gothruUserId uint64) — new. Calls recomputeAndSaveRanking(gothruUserId, preserveTimestamp=true), which uses .UpdateColumn("ranking", ranking) — UpdateColumn sets GORM's SkipHooks, which skips the auto-timestamp bump entirely.
  • BackfillRanking (maintenance.go) now calls RecomputeAndSaveRankingPreserveTimestamp instead of RecomputeAndSaveRanking.

Verification

  • Confirmed via actual emitted SQL (not just by reading the call site), per the issue's own explicit caveat that GORM's auto-timestamp behavior needed empirical confirmation.
  • TestRecomputeAndSaveRanking_BumpsUpdatedAt (computeRanking_ac3_test.go) — asserts the write-path SQL includes updated_at=?.
  • TestRecomputeAndSaveRankingPreserveTimestamp_DoesNotBumpUpdatedAt — asserts the backfill-path SQL omits updated_at entirely.
  • Checked all other references to photographers.updated_at in the codebase — none use it with a different meaning (no cache keys, sync jobs, exports, or SEO lastModified depending on it).
  • go build ./..., go vet ./... clean.

The penalty keys off photographers.updated_at. But most "profile sections" live in child tables, and writing them never touches the parent row.

Example — src/action/v1/portfolio/createPhotographerPortfolio.go:108 inserts into directory_portfolio and then only recomputes ranking:

    return models.DirectoryPortfolio{}, err
}
invalidateRedisCache(&photographer, identifier)
go photographers.RecomputeAndSaveRanking(photographer.GothruUserID)

photographers.updated_at is untouched. Same shape in:

  • src/action/v1/services/addPhotographerServices.go:92 / removePhotographerServices.go:71
  • src/action/v1/photographers/addPhotographerEquipment.go:102 / removePhotographerEquipment.go:71

Do not patch 16 call sites. All of them already call RecomputeAndSaveRanking, so one write there covers every path:

src/action/v1/photographers/computeRanking.go:135 currently does:

if err := config.GetConnPhotographers().Model(&p).Update("ranking", ranking).Error; err == nil {

Extend that update to also set updated_at. Single place, all callers fixed.

  • BackfillRanking calls the same function (src/action/v1/photographers/maintenance.go:105) in a loop over every photographer. If RecomputeAndSaveRanking starts bumping updated_at, running the backfill would mark every profile as freshly updated and wipe the penalty across the whole table. Needs a flag, a separate code path, or an explicit updated_at preservation in the backfill.
  • Confirm nothing else reads photographers.updated_at with a different meaning (cache keys, sync jobs, exports, SEO lastModified).

Issue #56 — Index Check for updated_at on the v2 Search Path

Status: Partial — code-level analysis complete, EXPLAIN blocked on live DB access
Type: Performance investigation
Depends on: #54

Scope

After #54, both ORDER BY and the keyset WHERE in /v2/photographers/users use a computed expression involving updated_at:

GREATEST(ranking - CASE WHEN (updated_at IS NULL OR updated_at < DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 365 DAY)) THEN 20 ELSE 0 END, 0)

The task: check existing indexes, EXPLAIN the query before/after, and confirm whether the expression forces a filesort at production row counts.

What was confirmed from the repo

  • No migration files exist anywhere in this repository (searched for any *migration* path — none found). Schema and indexes are managed outside this codebase.
  • DirectoryPhotographer (src/models/directory_photographer.go) has no index gorm tags on any field — only unique on gothru_user_id, slug, email. Neither ranking nor updated_at is declared indexed from the Go side, consistent with #52's finding that the pre-existing ORDER BY ranking DESC, rating_avg DESC, id DESC was already an unindexed filesort.
  • The post-#54 expression is a computed CASE/GREATEST expression, which no ordinary single-column index can serve directly — regardless of whether updated_at itself is indexed.

Blocked

This development environment has no reachable database — .env is absent (only .env.example with blank credentials), and there is no production-scale dataset available to test against. Running EXPLAIN or producing a real query plan without a live connection would mean fabricating numbers, which was avoided.

What's needed to close this out

Someone with access to DB_PHOTOGRAPHERS_* (staging or a production replica) needs to run:

EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM photographers
WHERE status IN (3,4)
ORDER BY GREATEST(ranking - CASE WHEN (updated_at IS NULL OR updated_at < DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 365 DAY)) THEN 20 ELSE 0 END, 0) DESC,
         rating_avg DESC, id DESC
LIMIT 20;

— both with and without the continentId/countryId/cityId joins from getPhotographers.go, at real row counts.

Recommendation if it does degrade

Because the expression can't be indexed as-is, the fix isn't a simple composite index — it would mean reopening #52 toward option B/C (a persisted, indexable column), which is exactly the tradeoff #52 already weighed and rejected for the cost of a migration + cron. Recommendation: ship #54 as shipped, measure with the query above, and only reopen #52 if the filesort is actually shown to matter at current row counts. Per #52's own note, latency on this query is more likely dominated by other factors — the dead cross-DB fetch (fixed in #59), cross-DB IN lists, and three Preloads.

issues.display_title: Issue #57: Ranking freshness: Redis cache serves pre-decay ordering past the 1-year boundary
issues.main_description_html:
Issue #57 — Redis Cache Serves Pre-Decay Ordering Past the 1-Year Boundary

Status: Done — measured and accepted, no code change
Type: Investigation / decision
Depends on: #54

Problem

Every existing cache invalidation for the v2 photographer list is write-triggered: RecomputeAndSaveRanking clears PhotographerListV2Pattern() on save. The freshness penalty has no write event — it flips purely because the clock passed 365 days — so a cached list page can keep serving pre-decay ordering indefinitely after a profile crosses the boundary, unless the cache naturally expires.

Findings

  • The PhotographerListV2 cache key TTL is a flat 24 hours (helpers.RedisCacheTTL = 60 * 60 * 24, src/helpers/redis_keys.go).
  • Confirmed ordering is baked in: GetPhotographers (src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers.go) serializes and caches the entire response map, including the ordered photographers array, keyed per (search, filters, cursor, size, cacheVersion) combination. So the stale-ordering window for any given cached page equals the TTL exactly, as predicted.
  • Confirmed every existing invalidation path is write-triggered — there is no independent expiry mechanism tied to the freshness boundary itself.

Decision: accepted, not reduced

The issue's own scope treats a short (minutes/hours) TTL as "bounded and acceptable — document it and close." 24 hours is within that bucket:

  • It's an existing, already-bounded TTL, not unbounded or absent — worst case is a once-per-cache-entry, up-to-24h-old view of one page slice, not permanent staleness.
  • Every cache key naturally re-populates with fresh ordering on its next miss regardless of writes — the drift self-corrects without manual intervention.
  • Adding a daily flush or shortening the TTL would trade a bounded, already-acceptable staleness window for either new scheduled-job infrastructure or more cache misses (and more DB load) on every page — for a decay effect that only matters on the exact day a given profile crosses the 1-year threshold. Not justified (YAGNI).

Outcome

No code change. Maximum staleness window: 24 hours, accepted explicitly and documented here and in the issue thread.

Parent: GoThruMedia/gothru-photographer-v2#17
Depends on: #54

Problem

Every existing cache invalidation is triggered by a write. RecomputeAndSaveRanking clears the list cache on save (src/action/v1/photographers/computeRanking.go:136):

_, _ = helpers.ClearRedisKeys(helpers.RedisKey.PhotographerListV2Pattern())

The freshness penalty has no write event — it flips purely because the clock passed 365 days. So a cached v2 list page can keep serving pre-decay ordering indefinitely after a profile crosses the boundary.

This is the same class of problem as #52, one layer up: time-dependent output behind a write-invalidated cache.

Scope

  • Find the TTL on PhotographerListV2Pattern keys. If it is short (minutes/hours), the drift is bounded and acceptable — document it and close.
  • If the TTL is long or absent, add a bounded expiry or a daily flush of the list cache.
  • Check whether getPhotographers v2 caches full serialized pages (ordering baked in) or just row data. If ordering is baked in, the stale-ordering window equals the TTL exactly.

Done when

Issue #58 — Tests for Decay, Boundary, Reset, and Pagination Stability

Status: Done — shipped in PR #60
Type: Test coverage
Depends on: #54, #55

Approach

All tests run against sqlmock (already used elsewhere in this repo — github.com/DATA-DOG/go-sqlmock) — no live database required. Exact SQL text for every mocked query was captured empirically (via a throwaway probe exploiting sqlmock's mismatch error, which prints the actual query GORM emits) rather than guessed, so the mocks reflect real GORM v1.31.1 output.

Freshness penalty (src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers_test.go)

Tests effectiveRanking directly, which mirrors the SQL expression used in production:

  • TestEffectiveRanking_FreshProfile_Unchanged — updated yesterday, across all tier baselines (0/20/40/60/79): score unchanged. Regression guard on existing behavior.
  • TestEffectiveRanking_StaleProfile_Penalised — 400 days stale: base - 20.
  • TestEffectiveRanking_StaleProfile_ClampsAtZero — low base minus penalty: clamps at 0, never negative.
  • TestEffectiveRanking_ExactlyOneYear_NotYetPenalised — exactly 365 days: fresh side of the boundary (<, not <=), asserted explicitly per #53.
  • TestEffectiveRanking_OneYearAndOneDay_Penalised — 366 days: penalised, confirming the boundary sits exactly where intended.
  • TestEffectiveRanking_NullUpdatedAt_TreatedAsStale — nil updated_at: penalised, no panic.

effectiveRanking takes an injected now time.Time specifically so the exact-boundary case is deterministic instead of racing the wall clock between test setup and the function call under test.

AC3 reset (src/action/v1/photographers/computeRanking_ac3_test.go, needs #55)

  • TestRecomputeAndSaveRanking_BumpsUpdatedAt — asserts the emitted SQL is UPDATE photographers SET ranking=?,updated_at=? ... (write paths reset the penalty).
  • TestRecomputeAndSaveRankingPreserveTimestamp_DoesNotBumpUpdatedAt — asserts UPDATE photographers SET ranking=? ... with no updated_at (what BackfillRanking now calls) — regression guard against the "backfill wipes every penalty" bug discovered while implementing #55.

A single test per code path was sufficient instead of one case per profile section: all 16 write-path callers funnel through the same RecomputeAndSaveRanking/recomputeAndSaveRanking function, so testing that one function covers every section, consistent with #55's single-choke-point fix.

v2 pagination (src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers_pagination_test.go, needs #54)

TestGetPhotographersV2_PagesAcrossFreshnessBoundary — seeds 3 photographers straddling the boundary (2 fresh, 1 stale) at page size 2, pages through the full set, and asserts:

  • Every photographer appears exactly once across both pages (rankings [60, 50] then [40] — no gaps or duplicates).
  • Ordering is monotonically non-increasing by effective ranking.
  • hasMore/nextCursor bookkeeping is correct on both pages.
  • The emitted SQL text (via ExpectQuery regexes) requires the literal GREATEST(ranking - CASE ... expression to appear in both the keyset WHERE and the ORDER BY — so reverting the ORDER BY back to raw ranking would fail this test.

Honest limit of this test

sqlmock never executes SQL — it can prove the Go code assembles the correct query text and correctly threads returned rows through the pagination bookkeeping (cursor effective score, response mapping, hasMore/nextCursor), but it cannot prove the SQL is semantically correct against a real MySQL engine (e.g. that GREATEST/CASE/DATE_SUB behave as expected). That would require an embedded MySQL instance or testcontainer, judged not worth the infrastructure cost for this change — the test comment states this limitation explicitly rather than overclaiming coverage.

Verification

go build ./..., go vet ./..., go test ./... all clean across the whole repository.

Issue #59 — v2 Photographer List: Dead Cross-DB User Fetch + Dead Tier Code

Status: Done — shipped in PR #60
Type: Bug fix / cleanup (unrelated to the ranking-freshness feature, filed separately)
Depends on: none — recommended to land before #54, since it touches the same function

Problem 1: wasted full-table cross-DB read on every non-search request

In GetPhotographers (src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers.go), the non-search branch fetched every GothruUser with subscribtion IN (1,2,5,6,7,8) from a second database connection (GetConnGothruMod) and then never read the result — the loop that built searchUserIds only appended when isSearch, and the WHERE gothru_user_id IN filter on the main query only applied when isSearch. The non-search branch is the default path (plain directory browse, homepage), so this fired on every request that missed the Redis cache.

Fix: moved the GothruUser fetch entirely inside if isSearch. Non-search requests no longer touch GetConnGothruMod() at all.

Problem 2: was the subscription filter meant to be applied?

The discarded else branch specifically selected subscribed tiers (1,2,5,6,7,8) — the same values tierBaseline treats as paid. Two possibilities needed resolving: the filter was obsolete (safe to delete), or it was supposed to be applied and free-tier photographers were leaking into the directory (a correctness bug).

Resolution: traced git history. Commit 287ec61 ("fix(v2): replace tier-based sort with ranking-based cursor pagination") deliberately removed the old tier-partitioned pagination scheme and its own commit message states: "Search filter (searchUserIds) preserved unchanged." Only the search-path fetch was meant to survive that refactor — the non-search subscribtion IN (...) fetch was leftover from the old scheme, never re-wired to filter anything after that commit. Confirmed dead, not a correctness bug: no subscription filtering was intended to apply to the plain directory/homepage browse path post-refactor. Recorded as a comment on #59 per the issue's own requirement, so it doesn't resurface as an open question later.

Problem 3: ~100 lines of dead tier-pagination code

getGreaterTierCondition, getSameTierCondition, and their only caller-of contains had no callers anywhere in the repository — leftovers from the tier-partitioned pagination scheme replaced by commit 287ec61's ranking-based keyset cursor. Deleted (~100 lines), making the remaining pagination logic (which #54 needed to modify) noticeably shorter and easier to reason about.

Verification

  • go build ./..., go vet ./... clean.
  • No behavior change: the non-search branch already applied no effective subscription filter before this change (the fetched users were never read in that branch); status IN (3,4) on DirectoryPhotographer is untouched; search-branch logic untouched.
  • Done ahead of #54 as recommended in the issue — the keyset cursor logic in this file was ~100 lines shorter before #54 touched it.

Found while scoping GoThruMedia/gothru-photographer-v2#17. Unrelated to that feature — filing separately.

This is the hottest read path in the service: getPhotographersV2 backs the directory page and the homepage in gothru-photographer-v2 (src/components/directory-page.tsx:166,189,228, src/app/page.tsx:86).

1. Every non-search request does a wasted full-table read across DB connections

src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers.go:169-211:

isSearch := search != ""
var users []models.GothruUser

if isSearch {
    err := config.GetConnGothruMod().Model(&models.GothruUser{}).
        Where("first_name LIKE ? OR last_name LIKE ?", "%"+search+"%", "%"+search+"%").
        Find(&users).Error
    // ...
} else {
    err := config.GetConnGothruMod().Model(&models.GothruUser{}).
        Where("subscribtion IN ?", []int{1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 8}).
        Find(&users).Error          // <-- line 193
    // ...
}

var searchUserIds []int
for _, u := range users {
    if isSearch {                   // <-- only populated when isSearch
        searchUserIds = append(searchUserIds, u.UserID)
    }
}

query := config.GetConnPhotographers().Model(&models.DirectoryPhotographer{}).
    Where("status IN ?", []int{3, 4})

if isSearch {
    query = query.Where("gothru_user_id IN ?", searchUserIds)   // <-- only used when isSearch
}

In the non-search branch, every GothruUser with subscribtion IN (1,2,5,6,7,8) is hydrated into memory from a second database connection (GetConnGothruMod), and then nothing reads it. The loop only appends when isSearch; the WHERE only applies when isSearch.

The non-search branch is the default path — plain directory browse and homepage. So this fires on every request that misses the Redis cache.

Fix: move the fetch inside the if isSearch branch. It is already there for the search case; the else branch just needs to be deleted.

2. Open question: was the subscription filter meant to be applied?

The else branch specifically selects subscribed tiers (1,2,5,6,7,8) — the same values tierBaseline treats as paid (src/action/v1/photographers/computeRanking.go:28-35). Someone wrote that filter deliberately, but its result is discarded, so the v2 list currently applies no subscription filter at all — only status IN (3,4).

Two possibilities, and they need different fixes:

  • The filter is obsolete → the fetch is simply dead, delete it (fix 1 above).
  • The filter was supposed to be applied → free-tier photographers are currently leaking into the directory listing, which is a correctness bug, and the fix is to apply it (ideally as a join or a persisted tier column, not an in-memory IN list).

Needs a decision before deleting. Check git history on this file for when the else branch stopped being used.

3. ~100 lines of dead tier-pagination code

getGreaterTierCondition (src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers.go:47-98) and getSameTierCondition (:100-138) have no callers anywhere in the repo. contains (:38-45) is used only by those two, so it dies with them.

They take subs58, subs16, subs27, premiumUserIds — leftovers from a tier-partitioned pagination scheme that the current ranking-based keyset cursor replaced. Deleting them removes roughly a quarter of the file and makes the remaining pagination logic readable, which matters because #54 has to modify exactly that logic.

Scope

  • Move the user fetch into the isSearch branch (pending the answer to §2).
  • Resolve §2 explicitly — record the answer in a comment either way.
  • Delete getGreaterTierCondition, getSameTierCondition, contains.
  • Confirm no behaviour change to the v2 response: same photographers, same order, same pagination.

Ordering vs #54

Worth doing before #54. That task edits the keyset cursor in this same function, and it is easier to reason about once the dead code is gone.

Done when

  • Non-search requests issue no query against GetConnGothruMod.
  • §2 answered in a comment.
  • Dead functions removed, go build and existing tests pass.
  • v2 list output verified unchanged.

Implementation — Migrate API Collection from Postman to Bruno

Status: Done
Depends on: postman-to-bruno-migration-task.md

Format

Collection uses Bruno's opencollection YAML format (not the older .bru
DSL). Root marker:

# api-collection/GoThru Maps/opencollection.yml
opencollection: 1.0.0
info:
  name: GoThru Maps
bundled: false
extensions:
  bruno:
    ignore:
      - node_modules
      - .git

Every folder gets a folder.yml with a seq (sidebar order) and, where the
whole folder shares auth, auth: inherit:

# v1 - photographers/folder.yml
info:
  name: v1 / photographers
  type: folder
  seq: 13
request:
  auth: inherit

Every request is its own <Request Name>.yml:

# v1 - photographers/Create Portfolio.yml
info:
  name: Create Portfolio
  type: http
  seq: 22
http:
  method: POST
  url: "{{base_url}}/v1/photographers/portfolio"
  auth: inherit
settings:
  encodeUrl: true
  timeout: 0
  followRedirects: true
  maxRedirects: 5
  forwardAuthorizationHeader: false

groups: v1 - availability, v1 - cron, v1 - equipment, v1 - geodata,

issues.display_title: Issue #66: [Role Profile] Task 1 - Schema, backfill, and seeds
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation Issue #66 — Role Profile: Schema, Backfill, and Seeds

Status: Done — shipped in PR #78 (9ac27d0)
Type: Schema change
Part of: #64
Depends on: none — runs first; every other task in the epic assumes these columns exist

Requirement

Add role, timezone, and language to photographers, a role column to services, catalog tables for languages and timezones, and the seed data the role rules depend on: five new services, equipment type 5 (Software), and one default row in each catalog.

Why an endpoint instead of a migration file

The design spec originally called for a hand-written SQL file in a migrations/ directory. The plan reversed that, and the plan is what shipped.

This repository has no migration tool, no migrations/ directory, and no precedent for schema change anywhere in its history. MySQL 8 has no ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS, so a raw SQL file cannot be made re-runnable without either a stored procedure or an out-of-band check. GORM's Migrator().HasColumn / AddColumn is idempotent and already a dependency, and the repository already exposes two comparable maintenance operations: POST /v1/photographers/maintenance/backfill-ranking and GET /v1/equipment/items/seed.

POST /v1/photographers/maintenance/migrate-role-profile

Registered in the static block of photographersRoutes.go, above the /:slug catch-all — Fiber would otherwise route it to GetPhotographersDetailBySlug.

What it does

src/action/v1/photographers/migrateRoleProfile.go, in order:

  1. photographers.role / timezone / language, each behind a HasColumn check.
  2. services.role, same guard.
  3. AutoMigrate for the two catalog tables.
  4. Backfills photographers rows where the new columns are NULL or ''.
  5. Seeds five services by exact name: Aerial/Drone Shooting, HDR Blending, Object Removal, Virtual Staging, Floor Plan Creation. Matching by name means a re-run reuses the existing row.
  6. Backfills services.role from helpers.RoleServiceNames.
  7. Seeds equipment id 5 = Software at an explicit id.
  8. Seeds languages with English and timezones with America/Toronto.

Every stage returns counts, so a second run can be shown to have changed nothing.

Two things it deliberately refuses to do

It will not rename an existing equipment type 5. If id 5 exists under another name, the migration logs a warning and leaves it alone. Renaming it would silently reassign every photographers_equipment row already filed under that type.

It will not guess a role for an unrecognized service. Any service whose name matches neither canonical list keeps a NULL role and is reported in servicesUnmapped. A wrong role here silently hides a service from the photographers who offer it. Such a service is visible in the flat catalog, absent from servicesByRole, and rejected by every assignment path until someone sets its role — which is what PUT /v1/services/:id is for (see #71).

Models

  • src/models/directory_photographer.go — Role, Timezone, Language.
  • src/models/directory_service.go — Role *string. A pointer, because a service can legitimately have no role until the backfill or an operator assigns one.
  • src/models/directory_language.go, directory_timezone.go — new.

language is text rather than varchar: MySQL forbids a DEFAULT on TEXT, so existing rows land as '' and step 4 backfills them. role and timezone carry quoted defaults, so their ALTER fills existing rows on its own.

Deploy order — the failure here is silent

Run the migration in production before the binary deploys. The failure mode is not an error, which makes it easy to miss:

  • GORM reads with SELECT *, so reads succeed and the missing columns scan as zero values.
  • Writes name the columns explicitly and fail.
  • An empty role makes helpers.RoleEquipmentTypes return nil, so type IN (?) becomes IN (NULL): equipment reads come back empty and every service and equipment write is rejected as role-incompatible.

The symptom is a photographer whose gear appears to have vanished, with nothing in the logs. (An earlier version of the PR description claimed reads would fail loudly with Unknown column 'role'; code review corrected that.)

Verification

  • go build ./..., go vet ./src/..., make test — clean.
  • Error handling on the seed lookups distinguishes gorm.ErrRecordNotFound from a transient failure, added after code review. Treating any error as "not found" would fall through to Create and insert a duplicate against the production schema.

Not verified end to end. The migration has never been executed against any database. Its idempotence is argued from the code, not demonstrated. Before running it in production, run it twice against a scratch copy of the schema: the second run must report 0 in every counter and no new servicesUnmapped entries.

Part of #64. Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-photographer-role-profile-api.md (#65).

Runs first. Every other task depends on these columns and seeds existing, and this has to be applied in production before the apply/profile changes ship.

Files

  • Modify: src/models/directory_photographer.go, src/models/directory_service.go, src/routes/v1/photographersRoutes.go
  • Create: src/models/directory_language.go, src/models/directory_timezone.go, src/action/v1/photographers/migrateRoleProfile.go, src/controllers/v1/photographers/migrateRoleProfile.go

Steps

  • Add to DirectoryPhotographer: Role string (column:role;type:varchar(32);not null;default:photographer_360), Timezone string (column:timezone;type:varchar(64);not null;default:America/Toronto), Language string (column:language;type:text;not null).
  • Add Role *string (column:role;type:varchar(32)) to DirectoryService.
  • Create DirectoryLanguage (languages: id, name varchar(100) unique) and DirectoryTimezone (timezones: id, name varchar(100) unique).
  • Write MigrateRoleProfile() — idempotent, returning a counts summary:
    1. For each of role, timezone, language: if !m.HasColumn(&models.DirectoryPhotographer{}, col) { m.AddColumn(...) }.
    2. Same guard for services.role.
    3. m.AutoMigrate(&models.DirectoryLanguage{}, &models.DirectoryTimezone{}).
    4. Backfill photographers: UPDATE photographers SET role='photographer_360' WHERE role IS NULL OR role='', same shape for timezone → America/Toronto and language → English.
    5. Seed missing services by exact name, reusing the existing row when the name is already there (see SeedEquipmentItems for the pattern): Aerial/Drone Shooting, HDR Blending, Object Removal, Virtual Staging, Floor Plan Creation.
    6. Backfill services.role from the canonical name→role map. Log any service name that maps to neither role instead of failing.
    7. Seed equipment row id=5 name Software (explicit id insert). Skip if id 5 exists; if it exists under another name, log it and leave it alone — do not silently rename another type.
    8. Seed languages with English and timezones with America/Toronto, insert-if-missing.
  • Controller + route: group.Post("/maintenance/migrate-role-profile", photographersController.MigrateRoleProfile), next to /maintenance/backfill-ranking and above the /:slug catch-all.

Why an endpoint and not a migration file

The repo has no migration tool, and MySQL 8 has no ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS. GORM's Migrator().HasColumn/AddColumn is idempotent and already a dependency, and an idempotent maintenance endpoint matches the existing /maintenance/backfill-ranking and GET /v1/equipment/items/seed.

Verification

  • Run the endpoint twice against a scratch DB — the second run reports 0 created and 0 altered.
  • No photographer row has an empty role, timezone, or language.

Risk

If equipment id 5 is already taken by a different type, the seed logs and skips. Check the target DB before running this in production.

issues.display_title: Issue #67: [Role Profile] Task 2 - Shared role rules helper
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation Issue #67 — Role Profile: Shared Role Rules Helper

Status: Done — shipped in PR #78 (9ac27d0)
Type: Feature
Part of: #64
Depends on: nothing at compile time; the DB-backed validators need #66's tables at runtime

Requirement

One place for every role rule, so no endpoint re-derives them. Eleven endpoints across three packages needed the same answers to "is this a valid role", "may this role own this equipment type", and "do these service ids belong to this role".

Why helpers and not action/v1/photographers

src/action/v1/services already imports src/action/v1/photographers. Putting role rules in photographers and then having photographers reach into services for the service-role check would close an import cycle. helpers already imports config, so DB-backed validation lives there without a new dependency edge.

Contents — src/helpers/photographerRole.go

Pure, no database:

IsValidRole(role string) bool
RoleEquipmentTypes(role string) []int8      // {1,2,3,4} or {5}
RoleAllowsEquipmentType(role string, t int8) bool
ParseLanguageCSV(csv string) ([]string, error)

Database-backed, kept separate so the pure ones stay unit-testable without a connection:

ValidateTimezone(name string) error
ValidateLanguages(csv string) error
ValidateServicesForRole(role string, ids []int) error
LoadRoleServices(ids []uint64, roleByID map[uint64]string) (map[uint64][]RoleServiceInfo, error)

RoleServiceNames is exported but used only by #66's migration to backfill services.role. Runtime checks read the column, never the name list — renaming a service in the database cannot silently break role rules.

Details worth knowing

RoleEquipmentTypes returns a copy. Callers pass the result straight into GORM's IN clause. Handing out the package-level slice would leave the rules one careless append away from corruption for every subsequent request. A test asserts the returned slice does not alias.

ParseLanguageCSV rejects blank tokens rather than dropping them. "English,," is an error, not a one-element list. Silently discarding the empty token would let a malformed payload persist as if it were valid (PRD §9).

ValidateLanguages compares against the de-duplicated request. "English,English" has two tokens but matches one row; comparing the row count to len(names) would reject a legitimate, if odd, input.

ValidateServicesForRole uses one query for two failure modes. COUNT(*) FROM services WHERE id IN (?) AND role = ? catches both "no such service" and "service belongs to the other role" — they are equally invalid at every call site, so distinguishing them would buy nothing.

LoadRoleServices filters in Go, not SQL. Every photographer in a page may have a different role, so a role-filtered SQL query would need one round trip per row. One IN (...) query plus an in-memory filter keeps it to a single trip. Added for #73, where both the dashboard and the v2 list needed it — the plan assigned the query to each endpoint separately; sharing it avoided two copies.

Implementation Issue #68 — Role Profile: Language and Timezone Catalog Endpoints

Status: Done — shipped in PR #78 (9ac27d0)
Type: Feature

Requirement

Expose the language and timezone catalogs so the dashboard can populate the two new required fields on apply and profile save with values the API will actually accept.

Endpoints

GET /v1/photographers/languages   ->  {"languages":[{"id":1,"name":"English"}]}
GET /v1/photographers/timezones   ->  {"timezones":[{"id":1,"name":"America/Toronto"}]}

Both ordered by name ASC, both cached at RedisCacheTTL under new keys AvailableLanguages(version) / AvailableTimezones(version), matching how GetAvailableServices caches. Both accept ?disablecache=true.

These are the only values ValidateTimezone and ValidateLanguages accept. language on apply and profile save is a comma-separated list drawn from this catalog; timezone is a single value.

Files

  • src/action/v1/photographers/catalogs.go — both actions, plus the shared CatalogItem shape.
  • src/controllers/v1/photographers/catalogs.go — both handlers.
  • src/routes/v1/photographersRoutes.go — both routes.
  • src/helpers/redis_keys.go — two new key builders.

Route placement matters

Both routes are registered in the STATIC block of photographersRoutes.go, alongside /services and /availability. The file ends with a catch-all:

group.Get("/:slug", photographersController.GetPhotographersDetailBySlug)

Fiber matches in registration order, so a route added below that line would never be reached — /v1/photographers/languages would be handled as a photographer whose slug is languages, returning 404 rather than the catalog.

Caching decision

The plan called for caching these; the design spec had argued against it, on the grounds that both tables hold a handful of rows and a Redis round trip costs more than the query. The plan won, for consistency with GetAvailableServices rather than on performance grounds — these are read on every dashboard profile form load, and the cost either way is negligible.

Neither endpoint has an invalidation path. The catalogs have no write endpoint, so rows change only through direct SQL or a future migration; a 24h TTL is the bound on how long a manually inserted language stays invisible. Worth revisiting only if a catalog write endpoint is ever added.

Requirement

POST /v1/photographers/apply requires role, timezone, and language, validates all three, persists them on the new photographer, and returns them (PRD R6–R8).

Changes

src/action/v1/photographers/applyPhotographer.go:

  • ApplyPhotographerRequest and ApplyPhotographerResponse each gain the three fields.
  • Validation runs alongside the existing checks, before the Gothru user lookup, all wrapped in ErrValidationFailed so the controller's existing 400 mapping applies unchanged:
    • helpers.IsValidRole(req.Role)
    • helpers.ValidateTimezone(req.Timezone)
    • helpers.ValidateLanguages(req.Language)
  • The three fields are set on the DirectoryPhotographer before Create.

src/controllers/v1/photographers/applyPhotographer.go — the response fiber.Map copies the three fields across.

The controller was missed on the first pass

The first commit added the fields to ApplyPhotographerResponse and stopped there. The controller does not marshal that struct; it rebuilds the response by hand:

"photographer": fiber.Map{
    "id":           data.ID,
    "gothruUserId": data.GothruUserID,
    ...
},

So the three fields were populated on the action's return value and then silently dropped before reaching the client — action tests would have passed, and the response was simply missing them. Caught in code review, fixed in 665bb53. The lesson is narrow but worth recording: in this codebase, a field on a response struct proves nothing about the response body until the controller is checked too.

Breaking change

An application that omits any of the three now returns 400. There is no default and no grace period — the PRD makes all three required, and a default would silently file every applicant under photographer_360.

issues.main_description_html:
Implementation Issue #70 — Role Profile: Profile GET and PATCH

Status: Done — shipped in PR #78 (c3db40f, cache loop corrected in 665bb53)
Type: Feature — breaking
Part of: #64
Depends on: #66, #67, #68

Requirement

GET /v1/photographers/:gothruUserId/profile returns the three new fields and only role-compatible services. PATCH requires role, timezone, language, and services on every save, validates services against the submitted role, and clears services and equipment when the role changes (PRD R16–R20).

GET

src/action/v1/photographers/getPhotographerProfile.go:

  • PhotographerProfileResponse gains role, timezone, language.
  • The services join gains AND services.role = ?, using the photographer's current role.

Assignments belonging to the other role stay in photographers_services but are not returned. They are hidden rather than deleted, so nothing is lost if the role changes back.

PATCH

src/action/v1/photographers/updatePhotographerProfile.go.

Role, Timezone, and Language are plain string on UpdateProfileRequest, not pointers, deliberately: an omitted field and an empty one are then indistinguishable, and both are rejected. Services keeps its *[]int type but changes meaning from optional to required, and must be non-empty.

Validation, all before the transaction opens so a bad request changes nothing:

  1. Role valid, else 400.
  2. Timezone in the catalog, else 400.
  3. Language CSV valid and every token in the catalog, else 400.
  4. services present and non-empty, else 400.
  5. helpers.ValidateServicesForRole(req.Role, *req.Services) — against the submitted role.

Step 5 replaced the previous "some services not found" existence check.

Validating against the submitted role is the whole point

Checking against the stored role would accept the old role's service ids during a role change and strand them immediately — invisible to every read and undeletable through the role-scoped delete. Checking against the submitted role means a role change must arrive with the new role's service ids in the same request, which is the only combination that leaves the photographer in a coherent state.

Transaction

roleChanged := req.Role != photographer.Role is computed before the transaction. Inside it, in order:

  1. Apply updates, now including the three new columns.
  2. If roleChanged, delete all photographers_equipment rows for this photographer.
  3. Delete and re-insert photographers_services (the existing block; services are now always supplied, so it always runs).
  4. Availability replacement and slug-history archiving, unchanged.

Equipment is cleared rather than hidden because the two roles share no equipment types — every existing item would be stranded, and the role-scoped delete in #72 would refuse to remove it. Equipment is never recreated by profile save; it is managed only through the equipment endpoints.

Cache

Profile save now also clears PhotographerServicesPattern, PhotographerEquipmentPattern, and PhotographerListV2Pattern. It replaces services on every save and can clear equipment, and none of those caches were being touched by a profile update before.

The first version of that loop iterated gothruUserId, photographer.ID, and the slug. Code review pointed out that the services and equipment keys are only ever built from the route identifier, the slug, or the gothruUserId — never the internal row id — so iterating photographer.ID cleared nothing. Removed in 665bb53, with a comment naming what the keys are built from so it does not get re-added.

Breaking change

Every client sending a partial patch — {"avatar": "..."} alone, for example — now receives 400. This follows PRD R17 directly; the non-breaking alternative (optional fields, defaults on omission) was considered and rejected in the design, because a default would silently assign a role.

Known behavior, accepted

services must contain at least one entry. The PRD calls this the "preferred rule for this release" rather than settling it, so it is an assumption: an empty array returns 400. Reversing it is a one-line change if product decides a role may have no selected service.

Verification

Not verified end to end. The plan's verification steps — a mismatched service id returns 400, a role change empties both photographers_services and photographers_equipment, the response carries the new role — require a live database and have not been run.

Imlementation Issue #71 — Role Profile: Role-Aware Services APIs

Status: Done — shipped in PR #78 (0033a5b, extended in 665bb53 and f0910ce)
Type: Feature
Part of: #64
Depends on: #66 (services.role), #67

Requirement

The available-services catalog becomes role-aware, and the per-photographer service endpoints only see, accept, and remove services matching the photographer's role (PRD R24–R28).

GET /v1/photographers/services

src/action/v1/services/getAvailableServices.go — signature becomes GetAvailableServices(role string, skipCache bool).

?role= Response
valid {"services": [...]} — only that role's services
invalid, non-empty 400
absent {"services": [...all...], "servicesByRole": {"photographer_360": [...], "image_processing": [...]}}

An unknown role returns 400 rather than falling back to the full list. A typo that silently returns everything looks like a working filter, which is worse than an error.

With no role, the flat services array is unchanged, so existing clients that iterate it keep working. servicesByRole is omitempty, so it does not appear on a filtered response.

The cache key gained a role segment — photographer:v%d:available-services:%s, with all when no role is given. Without it, a filtered response and the full list would collide in one key and be served interchangeably.

src/action/v1/redis/importToRedis.go was updated for the new signature; it warms the unfiltered variant.

GET /:identifier/services

Join gains AND services.role = ?. Historical assignments from the other role stay in the table and are not reported.

POST /:identifier/services

After the existing service lookup, the request is refused when service.Role does not match the photographer's role — new ErrServiceRoleMismatch, mapped to 400 by the controller. Assigning it would create a row the photographer can neither see nor delete, since both reads and deletes are role-scoped.

DELETE /:identifier/services/:serviceId

The assignment lookup now joins services and filters by the photographer's role, so a role-incompatible target returns ErrServiceAssignmentNotFound (404) and nothing is deleted — consistent with the reads, which do not show it either.

Code review checked the generated SQL for this join specifically: a bare SELECT * across it would have produced two id columns and risked deleting the wrong row. GORM qualifies the select to photographers_services.id, photographers_services.service_id, photographers_services.photographers_id, so there is no ambiguity.

POST and PUT /v1/services — added during review

Code review found that CreateService still inserted with role unset. Any service created after the migration would land as role = NULL: present in the flat catalog, absent from servicesByRole, and rejected by both AddPhotographerService and ValidateServicesForRole. Visible and unassignable.

  • POST /v1/services — role is now required and validated; 400 otherwise.
  • PUT /v1/services/:id — takes an optional role, empty meaning unchanged.

The PUT change was not requested by the review. It exists because #66's migration reports servicesUnmapped and the operator documentation says to review it — but with role assignable only at creation, the sole way to act on that report was manual SQL. A report that cannot be acted on through the API is not much of a report.

Cache invalidation gap — closed in f0910ce

ServicePattern clears service:v*:*. The photographer-facing catalog is keyed under photographer:v*:available-services:*. The two never overlapped, so GET /v1/photographers/services served a stale list for its full 24h TTL after any service was created, renamed, or deleted.

This predated the epic — a rename had always been invisible for a day — but making PUT /v1/services/:id the documented repair path for migration output turned it into a real problem. AvailableServicesPattern was added and is cleared from all three service mutations.

createService does not clear PhotographerServicesPattern the way update and delete do: a brand-new service is not assigned to anyone, so no photographer's service list can be affected.

Known behavior, accepted

A service stranded by a role change cannot be deleted through the API while the other role is active — the delete refuses it, by design, to stay consistent with the reads. The PRD puts an administrative cleanup path out of scope, and profile save (#70) already clears services in bulk on a role change, which is the main way such rows would appear.

Verification

  • go build ./..., go vet ./src/..., make test — clean.

Not verified end to end. The plan's checks — adding an image_processing service to a photographer_360 photographer returns 400, and the assigned-services read hides historical incompatible rows — require a live database and have not been run.

Implementation Issue #72 — Role Profile: Role-Aware Equipment APIs

Status: Done — shipped in PR #78 (0033a5b)
Type: Feature
Part of: #64
Depends on: #66 (equipment type 5 seed), #67

Requirement

Equipment reads, creates, and deletes are constrained to the types the photographer's role owns: 1–4 for photographer_360, 5 for image_processing (PRD R21–R23).

Type Name
1 Drone
2 360 Camera
3 DSLR
4 3D Scanner
5 Software

GET /:identifier/equipment

src/action/v1/photographers/getPhotographerEquipment.go — the gear query gains AND type IN ? from helpers.RoleEquipmentTypes(photographer.Role), and the hardcoded typeMap gains 5: "Software".

Making typeMap database-backed was considered and left out of scope: it was already hardcoded before this epic, and the PRD does not ask for it.

POST /:identifier/equipment

The old guard was:

if req.Type < 1 || req.Type > 4 {
    return nil, errors.New("type must be between 1 and 4")
}

Two problems. It hardcoded the range, and it ran before the photographer was loaded, so it could not know the role. The photographer lookup moved above the check, which is now:

if !helpers.RoleAllowsEquipmentType(photographer.Role, req.Type) {
    return nil, fmt.Errorf("equipment type %d is not allowed for role %s (allowed: %v)", ...)
}

The error names the types the role does allow, so a rejected request says what would have worked. Name-length, brand-length, and duplicate checks are unchanged.

DELETE /:identifier/equipment/:itemId

The lookup gains AND type IN ? for the role's types, so a role-incompatible item returns ErrEquipmentNotFound and nothing is deleted — matching what the read shows.

Interaction with a role change

Because all three operations are role-scoped, an item left behind by a role change would be invisible and undeletable. That is why #70's profile save deletes photographers_equipment outright when the role changes, rather than hiding those rows the way services are hidden. Services survive a role change because a photographer switching back would want them; equipment cannot survive, because no type is shared between the two roles.

The consequence is worth stating plainly: a role change destroys the photographer's equipment list. It is not recoverable through the API. This follows from the PRD's role model rather than from an implementation choice, but it is the most destructive behavior in the epic.

Verification

  • go build ./..., go vet ./src/..., make test — clean.

Not verified end to end. The plan's checks — type 5 on a photographer_360 returns 400, type 5 on an image_processing is created, historical types 1–4 are invisible to an image_processing photographer — require a live database and have not been run.

issues.main_description_html:
Implementation Issue #74 — Role Profile: Cache Invalidation

Status: Done — shipped in PR #78 (6865899, plus 665bb53 and f0910ce)
Type: Chore
Part of: #64
Depends on: #70, #71, #73

Requirement

Every cached response whose shape changed in this epic must stop serving the old shape once the new binary is live (PRD R32).

Version bump, and why the literals had to go

helpers.DefaultCacheVersion went from 1 to 2. Because the version is part of every key, old keys are simply never read again and expire on their own TTL — no flush, no new code.

That only works for call sites that pass the constant. Several passed a literal:

getPhotographerEquipment.go   PhotographerEquipment(identifier, 1)      x3
getPhotographerProfile.go     PhotographerDetail(..., 1)
getPhotographerServices.go    PhotographerServices(identifier, 0)
getPhotographersDashboard.go  Version: 2

Bumping the constant alone would have left those keys untouched, still serving responses without the new fields — and the next bump would have hit the same bug. All of them now pass helpers.DefaultCacheVersion.

getPhotographersMarkersByLocation.go also passed a literal 1. Markers do not carry any of the new fields, so it needed no invalidation, but it was changed too: leaving one literal behind reintroduces exactly the trap this task exists to remove. The cost is one extra repopulation of the markers cache after deploy.

Write-path invalidation

Profile save (#70) now clears PhotographerServicesPattern, PhotographerEquipmentPattern, and PhotographerListV2Pattern in addition to what it already cleared. It replaces services on every save and can clear equipment on a role change, and none of those caches were being touched by a profile update before.

The first version of that loop also iterated photographer.ID. Code review found it cleared nothing — services and equipment keys are built from the route identifier, the slug, or the gothruUserId, never the internal row id. Removed in 665bb53.

Service mutations (#71) had a gap that predated the epic. ServicePattern clears service:v*:*; the photographer-facing catalog is keyed under photographer:v*:available-services:*. The two never overlapped, so GET /v1/photographers/services served a stale list for its full 24h TTL after any create, rename, or delete. Closed in f0910ce with a new AvailableServicesPattern, cleared from all three mutations.

New key shapes

  • AvailableServices takes a role: photographer:v%d:available-services:%s, with all when unfiltered. Without the segment, a ?role=-filtered response and the full list would share one key.
  • AvailableLanguages / AvailableTimezones — new, from #68.
  • AvailableServicesPattern — new, carrying a comment explaining why it is distinct from ServicePattern, since that distinction is exactly what was missed before.

What is still stale after deploy, and for how long

Nothing that matters — the version bump covers every changed shape. The bound on any remaining staleness is RedisCacheTTL, 24 hours. Requests can be forced past the cache with ?disablecache=true while spot-checking a deploy.

Verification

  • go build ./..., go vet ./src/..., make test — clean.
  • grep -rn --include="*.go" -E "helpers\.RedisKey\.[A-Za-z]+\(.*, ?[0-9]+\)|Version: *[0-9]+" src/ returns no non-test matches.

Not verified end to end. The plan's check — after a deploy against a warm Redis, every affected endpoint returns the new fields on the first request — requires a deploy and has not been performed.

Steps

  • DefaultCacheVersion = 2.
  • Replace hardcoded version literals with helpers.DefaultCacheVersion at the affected call sites — at minimum PhotographerDetail(..., 1) in getPhotographerProfile.go, PhotographerEquipment(..., 1) in getPhotographerEquipment.go, and Version: 2 in getPhotographersDashboard.go. Find the rest with:
grep -rn --include="*.go" -E "helpers\.RedisKey\.[A-Za-z]+\(.*, ?[0-9]+\)|Version: *[0-9]+" src/

Why both halves

getVersion() only falls back to DefaultCacheVersion when the caller passes 0. Call sites that pass a literal 1 or 2 today would keep their old keys after the bump, serve stale payloads missing the new fields, and hit the same bug on the next bump. Replacing the literals is the root-cause fix.

they expire (RedisCacheTTL) or a write-triggered invalidation overwrites
them.

No invalidation mechanism was added — bounded, self-correcting staleness,
same acceptance reasoning as
docs/implementation/issue-57-redis-cache-staleness.md. The write path is
already correct: AddPhotographerAvailability and
RemovePhotographerAvailability both clear
RedisKey.PhotographerDetailPattern for the identifier, slug, and gothru user
ID, so any availability edit repopulates the entry with the new shape
immediately.

{"data":{"availabilities":[{"day":"sunday","id":1},...,{"day":"saturday","id":7}],

Type: Bug
Source: gothru-photographer-v2#27
— "Handle Issue Data Availability Profile Does Not Match the Dashboard and
Database", sample photographer id = 102

Problem

The public photographer profile at 360photographers.org/photographer/:slug
showed availability that contradicted both the GoThru dashboard and the
database. For photographer id = 102, the photographer_availabilities table
holds all seven days and the dashboard displays them correctly, while the
public profile rendered Sunday as Closed, Monday–Friday as Open, and no
Saturday row at all.

The cause is in this repository: GET /v1/photographers/:slug never selected
availability, so the field was absent from the response entirely — not an
empty array, the key was missing. The frontend, having no data to render,
fell back to a hardcoded six-day array. That fallback was what users saw, and
it would have shown the same six rows regardless of what the database held.

Only the public detail endpoint was incomplete.

Add availability to the GET /v1/photographers/:slug response so the public
profile can render the same days the dashboard and database already agree on.

    consistent.

    column (sunday…saturday). No casing translation in the API — presentation
    casing belongs to the consumer.

    An absent or null field is indistinguishable from "closed" downstream, and
    the frontend has to be able to tell "no data" from "not available".
  • No new column or migration — reuse the existing availabilities and
    photographer_availabilities tables.
  • Additive only; no change to the existing response shape.

Out of scope

    returning the old shape until RedisCacheTTL expires or a write-triggered
    invalidation overwrites them. Same accepted, self-correcting staleness as
    docs/implementation/issue-57-redis-cache-staleness.md.
  • The write path for availability. AddPhotographerAvailability and
    RemovePhotographerAvailability already invalidate the photographer detail
    cache keys correctly; nothing there needed changing.

Update the automated sitemap generator for 360photographers.org to exclude test user profiles and explicitly include essential static pages (/about, /contact).

What excluding test <> '0' would actually do

Joined against 360directory.photographers (165 published profiles today):

test photographer rows published (status 3/4)
1 8 3
2 0 0
4 0 0
7 17 7

That is 10 of 165 published profiles removed — 6% of the directory. And they do not look like test data: zero test-shaped slugs among them, 9 of 10 have avatars, 7 of 10 have websites, and one has real reviews.

Meanwhile the flag misses the actual test account

Six photographer rows have genuinely test-shaped slugs (test-, -test-, test-acc). Five are unpublished. One is live:

slug = test-address-nlxn
gothru_user_id = 54362
users.test = 0

I pulled all 165 slugs directly from GET /v2/photographers/users — test-address-nlxn is in the public directory right now, and would be published into sitemap.xml. users.test = '0', so a test <> '0' filter does not touch it.

So the flag would delete 10 real-looking profiles and still leave the one real test profile listed. It reads more like a gothru-side account categorisation than a directory test marker — whoever owns that column should confirm what 1, 2, 4 and 7 mean.

Where the sitemap leak actually came from

Not the test flag. sitemap.xml was generated from the v1 photographer list, the last caller left on that endpoint. v1 returns unpublished rows and overlapping pages, which is why test profiles appeared there: of 337 URLs, 123 were duplicates and 120 returned HTTP 404.

GoThruMedia/gothru-photographer-v2#34 switches the generator to v2 and deduplicates. v2's existing status IN (3,4) filter already drops five of the six test-slug rows, and the sitemap goes to 210 unique URLs with 202 returning 200.

  2. AC1 (no test profiles) — effectively closed by the same PR, with one exception: test-address-nlxn needs its status changed so it leaves the directory. That is an ops action, no code required.
  3. No users.test filter. I built and tested one (shared helper, nine public readers, sqlmock tests, all green) and am not proposing it — on this data it costs 10 real profiles and fixes nothing the v2 switch did not already fix. If a durable marker is wanted, an explicit is_test column on 360directory.photographers that ops can set would be the honest version, but that is a separate issue.

The remaining 8 sitemap URLs that still 404 are unrelated to test accounts — non-ASCII slugs, filed as #81.
