issues.display_title: Issue #86: Filter City Queries to Only Return Cities With Active Photographers
issues.main_description_html:
PR #88: Active City Filtering — Final Implementation

Metadata

  • Issue: #86 — Filter City Queries to Only Return Cities With Active Photographers
  • Pull request: #88 — Implement active city filtering in GetCities and SearchLocation
  • Merge commit: f4665469876bfcdf5ba096292aaa3de28a6390ef
  • Status: merged to main on 2026-09-03

Result

City listing and location search now return only cities served by at least one approved photographer. A city qualifies through either the photographer's primary city or one of their sublocations.

The implementation also keeps cached city membership current, returns empty collections consistently when no active city matches, and preserves existing nearest-city behavior for callers outside the public city endpoint.

Active City Definition

geodata.ActiveCities is the shared GORM scope used by both city listing and location search. It joins city against the union of:

  1. Primary photographer locations where:
    • photographers.status = 3 (approved)
    • city_id is present
    • latitude and longitude are present
  2. Photographer sublocations where:
    • the linked photographer has status = 3
    • the sublocation has latilatitude and longitude

Using one shared scope prevents GetCities and SearchLocation from defining active membership differently. SQL UNION removes duplicate city IDs before the join.

City Listing

src/action/v1/geodata/getCities.go now:

  • applies ActiveCities before country and name filters;
  • accepts an unfiltered request and returns all active cities;
  • converts URL-style names such as new-york to a case-insensitive database search for new york;
  • loads photographer counts in one bulk query;
  • skips any city whose count becomes zero between the active-city query and count query.

The final zero-count check is a race guard. It handles status or location changes that occur while the request is running.

Location Search

src/action/v1/photographers/searchLocation.go now:

  • applies the same ActiveCities scope;
  • keeps the existing country and continent joins and 20-city limit;
  • loads city, country, and continent counts in bulk;
  • propagates city-count query errors instead of returning incomplete results;
  • skips a city if its active count becomes zero during the request;
  • returns an allocated empty results array when no city matches.

Existing validation remains unchanged: q must contain at least two characters after trimming.

GET /v1/geodata/cities Behavior

The controller supports these inputs:

  • no filter: all active cities;
  • countryId: active cities in one country;
  • name: active city name search with slug normalization;
  • latlong: nearest-city lookup followed by an active photographer count check.

Response behavior:

  • invalid latlong: 400;
  • query or count failure: 500;
  • no matching city: 200 with {"cities": []};
  • matching city data: 200 with city ID, name, and active photographer count.

The old record not found branches were removed because they were unreachable: GORM Find returns an empty slice, while GetNearestCity converts gorm.ErrRecordNotFound to (nil, nil).

Nearest-City Decision

The latlong path intentionally keeps using the unfiltered GetNearestCity. The controller then omits that city when its active count is zero.

Therefore, a user closest to an inactive city receives an empty array instead of the next-nearest active city. A separate GetNearestActiveCity entry point was not added because other GetNearestCity callers must continue resolving inactive cities during photographer application and location editing.

Cache Strategy

Response namespaces changed so previously cached unfiltered data is never reused:

  • city listing: geodata:v{version}:active-cities...
  • location search: search:v{version}:active-location:{query}

RedisKey.SearchPattern() returns search:v*:*.

Every existing GeodataPattern() invalidation now also clears SearchPattern(). This covers 14 mutation paths across:

  • photographer application, deletion, equipment, location, and status changes;
  • approved-to-pending reversion after profile changes;
  • availability changes;
  • service changes;
  • sublocation creation, update, and deletion.

RevertApprovedToPendingOnSave clears both geodata and search caches only after the status update succeeds. This prevents a city from remaining searchable for the 24-hour Redis TTL after its last approved photographer becomes pending.

Coverage includes:

  • unfiltered active city listing;
  • slug-to-database-name mapping;
  • primary and sublocation active membership;
  • zero-count race guards;
  • inactive nearest-city omission;
  • empty results for missing city data;
  • city-count error propagation;
  • active cache key namespaces and search invalidation pattern;
  • geodata and search invalidation after approved-to-pending reversion.

The reversion test uses the installed go-redis/v9 hook API to observe production SCAN patterns without adding a Redis test dependency or starting a network server.

issues.display_title: Issue #89: Photographer detail 404s for the non-ASCII slugs the list and redirect endpoints emit
issues.main_description_html:
Description

GET /v1/photographers/:slug only resolves the ASCII-folded form of a slug (jorg-halisch-yk06), but GET /v2/photographers/users and GET /v1/photographers/slugs?redirect= both emit the accented form (jörg-halisch-yk06) with isRedirect: false.

Every link the site produces for these photographers — directory cards, the map list, /sitemap.xml — therefore points at a URL that 404s. 8 of 165 published profiles are unreachable this way, on production today.

slug as emitted by v2 list / redirect lookup /v1/photographers/:slug ASCII-folded form /v1/photographers/:slug
jörg-halisch-yk06 404 jorg-halisch-yk06 200
jose-mª-laffitte-29pr 404 jose-ma-laffitte-29pr 200
frédéric-lipzyc-py6b 404 frederic-lipzyc-py6b 200
gabriel-latorre-gonçalves-uxo4 404 gabriel-latorre-goncalves-uxo4 200
martin-hrdlička-k3xd 404 martin-hrdlicka-k3xd 200
filip-pavlíček-pdd5 404 filip-pavlicek-pdd5 200
martin-šturcel-lwd3 404 martin-sturcel-lwd3 200
miguel-goiás-4sg6 404 miguel-goias-4sg6 200

Folded = NFKD normalisation with combining marks dropped. Every other URL variant tried (percent-encoded, NFD, oe transliteration) also 404s.

Reproduce

B=http://<api-host>:3008
# what the list emits
curl -s "$B/v2/photographers/users?size=100" | jq -r '.data.photographers[].slug' | grep -P '[^\x00-\x7F]'
# the redirect lookup agrees with the list and says it is canonical
curl -s "$B/v1/photographers/slugs?redirect=j%C3%B6rg-halisch-yk06"
# {"data":{"gothruUserId":2422,"slug":"jörg-halisch-yk06","fullname":"Jörg Halisch","isRedirect":false}}
# but the detail endpoint cannot resolve it
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" "$B/v1/photographers/j%C3%B6rg-halisch-yk06"   # 404
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" "$B/v1/photographers/jorg-halisch-yk06"        # 200

Same on production: https://360photographers.org/photographer/j%C3%B6rg-halisch-yk06 → 404.

Likely cause

The slug is stored or matched in its folded form for the detail lookup, while the list and the redirect lookup return the un-folded display value (or vice versa). The three code paths disagree on what the canonical slug is.

Suggested fix

Pick one canonical form and make all three endpoints agree. Two options, not exclusive:

  1. Detail endpoint folds the incoming slug before lookup. Smallest change, and tolerant of both forms already in the wild.
  2. List and redirect endpoints emit the folded slug. If slugs?redirect= returns { "slug": "jorg-halisch-yk06", "isRedirect": true } for the accented input, the frontend's existing proxy already 301s old links to the working URL with no frontend change (src/proxy.ts checkPhotographerRedirect).

Acceptance criteria

  1. Every slug returned by GET /v2/photographers/users resolves with 200 on GET /v1/photographers/:slug.
  2. GET /v1/photographers/slugs?redirect=<accented form> either resolves as canonical or returns the canonical slug with isRedirect: true.
  3. All 8 profiles above load on 360photographers.org/photographer/<slug> from the directory, the map, and /sitemap.xml.

Context

Found while verifying GoThruMedia/gothru-photographer-v2#43 (sitemap for #87): every URL in /sitemap.xml was curled against a production build, and these 8 were the only failures left. Frontend passes the slug through unchanged; nothing to fix there until the API agrees with itself.

Description

Image processing profiles on the frontend (/image-processing/[slug]) render a "Professional Services" section: one tile per service, each with an icon, a name and an optional "View Sample" link. issues.display_title: Issue #103: Table-backed delayed queue and spam scoring for directory inquiries
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation Record: Table-Backed Delayed Queue and Anti-Spam Scoring for Directory Inquiries

Metadata

  • Issues:
    • #101 — Implement Delayed Queue and Anti-Spam Scoring System for Directory Inquiries
    • #103 — Table-backed delayed queue and spam scoring for directory inquiries
  • Pull Request: #105 — Table-backed delayed queue and spam scoring for directory inquiries
  • Date: 2026-09-16
  • Status: Implemented & Verified

1. Problem & Context

Photographers listed in the directory were receiving automated bot spam campaigns (such as unsolicited artwork purchase solicitation templates).

Previously, POST /v1/photographers/:slug/contact handled submissions completely synchronously:

  • Immediately called helpers.SendEmail via the Plunk API.
  • Had no delay buffer between submission and email delivery.
  • Performed no submission rate limiting (by IP or email).
  • Had no duplicate text detection or IP capture.
  • Did not persist inquiry records, leaving no audit or administrative trail for review.

2. Architecture & Design Decisions

Storage Choice: Table-Backed MySQL Queue

Pending inquiries and blocked messages are persisted in a new MySQL table (photographers_inquiries) on the photographers database. Redis is used exclusively for rate-limiting counters.

Rejected Alternatives:

  1. RabbitMQ TTL + Dead-Letter Exchange (DLX):
    • The repository has no queue declaration logic in src/lib/rabbitmq/rabbitmq.go (it only publishes and consumes existing queues).
    • Would require external ops provisioning of exchanges and queues, blocking deployment.
    • Leaves nowhere to store administrative audit/review records for blocked spam.
  2. Redis Sorted Set (Delay Queue):
    • Routine cache clear operations (POST /v1/redis/clear) accept arbitrary patterns and would wipe pending inquiries.
    • Concurrency race conditions: ZRangeByScore followed by ZRem is non-atomic, creating double-send risks.
    • MySQL InnoDB provides atomic row claims (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE), transaction rollback safety, and persistent review records.

3. Database Schema

Defined in sql/2026-09-16-create-photographers-inquiries.sql:

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `photographers_inquiries` (
  `id` INT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `photographer_id` BIGINT NOT NULL,
  `client_name` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  `client_email` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  `client_message` TEXT NOT NULL,
  `ip` VARCHAR(45) NULL,
  `body_hash` CHAR(64) NOT NULL,
  `spam_score` INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  `spam_reasons` TEXT NULL,
  -- pending | sending | sent | blocked | failed
  `status` VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
  `send_after` TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
  `sent_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
  `created_at` TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `idx_photographers_inquiries_dispatch` (`status`, `send_after`),
  KEY `idx_photographers_inquiries_body_hash` (`body_hash`, `created_at`),
  CONSTRAINT `fk_photographers_inquiries_photographer`
    FOREIGN KEY (`photographer_id`) REFERENCES `photographers` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

Model Mapping

The GORM model is defined in src/models/directory_photographer_inquiry.go as DirectoryPhotographerInquiry, mapping to photographers_inquiries.

4. Anti-Spam Scoring Pipeline

Implemented in src/action/v1/photographers/inquirySpamScore.go.

Thresholds & Constants

  • InquiryDelayDuration = 30 * time.Minute
  • SpamScoreThreshold = 50
  • MaxInquiriesPerIPPerHour = 5
  • MaxInquiriesPerEmailPerHour = 3
  • DuplicateOtherSendersThreshold = 2 (At least 2 other distinct senders, i.e., 3 senders total with the same body = template blast)
  • DuplicateSameEmailThreshold = 5 (More than 5 identical bodies sent by the same email within 24 hours)
  • MinBodyLengthForDuplicateCheck = 50 (Short generic messages under 50 characters are exempted from duplicate text matching to prevent false positives)

Scoring Signals

  1. Normalized Message Hashing (ComputeBodyHash):
    • Normalizes whitespace and converts text to lowercase: strings.Join(strings.Fields(strings.ToLower(msg)), " ").
    • Computes SHA-256 hex string (CHAR(64)).
  2. Hourly Rate Limits (via Redis with 1-hour TTL):
    • Per IP: inq:ip:<ip> (INCR with 1-hour expiration on first key creation). If n > 5, adds +50 score.
    • Per Sender Email: inq:email:<normalized_email> (INCR with 1-hour expiration). If n > 3, adds +50 score.
  3. Cross-Sender Template Blast Detection (MySQL 24-hour window):
    • Queries COUNT(DISTINCT client_email) for matching body_hash within 24 hours, excluding the current sender and excluding already blocked rows (status != 'blocked').
    • If >= 2 other senders have submitted the exact same message body (and length >= 50), adds +50 score.
    • Legitimate clients emailing multiple photographers with the same project brief (1–3 photographers) are permitted and not flagged.
  4. Excessive Single-Sender Duplication:
    • If the same email submits the exact same message body to > 5 photographers within 24 hours, adds +50 score.
  5. Silent Blocking & API Response:
    • If spam_score >= 50, the inquiry row is inserted with status = 'blocked'.
    • The API returns 200 OK with {"message": "Contact message sent successfully"} for both pending and blocked inquiries, preventing bots from inferring detection thresholds.

5. Delayed Queue Dispatch Worker

Implemented in src/action/v1/photographers/dispatchInquiries.go.

Execution Flow

  1. Reclaiming Stale Claims:
    • At the beginning of each tick, any inquiries stuck in sending state for more than 10 minutes (updated_at < NOW() - 10 MINUTE) are automatically reset back to pending. This recovers from worker crashes or deploys without stranded rows.
  2. Atomic Row Claiming:
    • Uses an InnoDB transaction with SELECT ... WHERE status = 'pending' AND send_after <= NOW() LIMIT 50 FOR UPDATE.
    • Transitions claimed row IDs to status = 'sending'.
  3. Dispatch Re-evaluation (Sender-Own Rate Limit Re-check):
    • Before dispatching an email, the worker re-evaluates the sender's own email rate limit counter (inq:email:<email>) without incrementing it.
    • If the sender subsequently flooded inquiries after their initial submission, their earlier pending inquiries are caught and updated to status = 'blocked'.
    • Cross-sender checks and IP checks are omitted at dispatch to avoid retroactive false positives on shared network addresses (NAT / CGNAT).
  4. Email Dispatch:
    • Queries photographer contact details (id, email, fullname).
    • Calls sendInquiryEmail(photographer.Email, CONTACT_TEMPLATE_ID, payload).
    • On success: marks row as status = 'sent', recording sent_at = NOW().
    • On failure: marks row as status = 'failed'.

6. Gateway & IP Resolution

  • In src/controllers/v1/photographers/contactPhotographer.go, the client IP is extracted directly via c.Get("X-Real-IP").
  • If the gateway does not forward X-Real-IP, ip safely defaults to an empty string, gracefully skipping IP rate limiting and falling back to email rate limits and duplicate checks (avoiding shared counter collisions on gateway proxy addresses).
  • Fiber app configuration remains minimal and untouched, preserving standard logger ${ip} output.

7. API Process Integration & Graceful Shutdown

In cmd/api/main.go:

  • The queue worker runs on a 1-minute ticker inside a background goroutine on non-child Fiber processes (!fiber.IsChild()).
  • The worker listens on a tickerDone channel and cleanly exits when the application receives SIGINT / SIGTERM before database pools close.

8. Changed & Added Files

File Purpose

src/models/directory_photographer_inquiry.go GORM model definition
src/helpers/redis_keys.go Added InquiryRateLimitIP and InquiryRateLimitEmail key helpers

9. Deployment Instructions

  1. Database Migration (Manual):
    This repository has no automated migration runner. The SQL script must be executed manually on the target photographers MySQL database before deploying the new binary: 
    mysql -u <user> -p photographers < sql/2026-09-16-create-photographers-inquiries.sql
  2. Reverse Proxy / Gateway Configuration:
    Ensure the edge proxy/gateway forwards the client IP in the X-Real-IP header (proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;).
  3. Deploy Application:
    Deploy and restart backend processes. Stranded rows from prior deployments will automatically be reclaimed after 10 minutes.

10. Verification

# Run all unit and integration tests
go test -count=1 ./...

# Verify code analysis
go vet ./...

# Verify build
go build ./...

# Verify code formatting
gofmt -l src/ cmd/

All checks completed with 100% pass rate and zero warnings.

Implementation task for #101, scoped to the table-backed approach.

Decision

Pending inquiries and blocked-message records are stored in a new MySQL table on the photographers database. Redis is used only for rate-limit counters and duplicate-body detection.

Two alternatives were considered and rejected:

  • RabbitMQ TTL + dead-letter queue. This repo contains no QueueDeclare anywhere — src/lib/rabbitmq/rabbitmq.go only publishes and consumes, and assumes queues already exist. The delay queue and its DLX would have to be created by whoever administers RabbitMQ, outside this codebase, so the work blocks on ops. It also leaves the admin review record from #101 with nowhere to live.
  • Redis-only (sorted set as delay queue). Fewest files, but POST /v1/redis/clear (src/controllers/v1/redis/clearKeys.go:23) accepts an arbitrary pattern, so a routine cache wipe would silently delete pending inquiries. Everything currently in Redis is cache that can be rebuilt from the database; an inquiry cannot. ZRangeByScore followed by ZRem is also not atomic, so two workers can send the same email twice. A table gets an atomic claim for free from UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'pending'.

Current behaviour

POST /v1/photographers/:slug/contact → src/action/v1/photographers/contactPhotographer.go:44 is fully synchronous: validate, look up the photographer, call helpers.SendEmail. There is no delay, no rate limiting, no IP capture, and no record of the submission.

Schema

New table, following the convention in sql/2026-09-11-create-photographers-professional-services.sql (MySQL, run by hand — this repo has no migration tool).

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `photographers_inquiries` (
  `id` INT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `photographer_id` BIGINT NOT NULL,
  `client_name` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  `client_email` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  `client_message` TEXT NOT NULL,
  `ip` VARCHAR(45) NULL,
  `body_hash` CHAR(64) NOT NULL,
  `spam_score` INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  `spam_reasons` TEXT NULL,
  -- pending | sent | blocked | failed
  `status` VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
  `send_after` TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
  `sent_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
  `created_at` TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `idx_photographers_inquiries_dispatch` (`status`, `send_after`),
  KEY `idx_photographers_inquiries_body_hash` (`body_hash`, `created_at`),
  CONSTRAINT `fk_photographers_inquiries_photographer`
    FOREIGN KEY (`photographer_id`) REFERENCES `photographers` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

Model goes in src/models/directory_photographer_inquiry.go as DirectoryPhotographerInquiry, matching the existing Directory* naming.

Spam scoring

One function returning an additive int plus the reasons that contributed. No rule engine, no ML.

  • Duplicate body — SHA-256 of the normalised message (lowercased, whitespace collapsed), counted against body_hash over the last 24 hours.
  • Rate limit per IP and per email — Redis INCR with EXPIRE on first hit, hourly window: 
    n, _ := config.Redis.Incr(ctx, "inq:ip:"+ip).Result()
if n == 1 { config.Redis.Expire(ctx, "inq:ip:"+ip, time.Hour) }
  • IP reputation — see the open question below. Ship phase one with per-IP counters only.

Above the threshold, the row is written with status = 'blocked' and no email is sent. The API response stays identical either way, so a bot cannot tell it was filtered.

Dispatch

Ticker riding the API process rather than a fourth worker binary. The repo has no deploy manifests, so a new binary means someone has to start it on the server; a goroutine means no deploy change at all.

// ponytail: ticker rides the API process, move to cmd/workers/ if volume grows
if !fiber.IsChild() {
    go func() {
        for range time.Tick(time.Minute) { photographers.DispatchPendingInquiries() }
    }()
}

fiber.IsChild() guards against prefork (APP_FORK_MODE=true) running the ticker once per child. Claim rows with UPDATE ... SET status = 'sending' WHERE status = 'pending' AND send_after <= NOW() before sending, so a double-start cannot send twice.

Files

  • sql/<date>-create-photographers-inquiries.sql — new
  • src/models/directory_photographer_inquiry.go — new
  • src/action/v1/photographers/inquirySpamScore.go — new
  • src/action/v1/photographers/contactPhotographer.go — record instead of send
  • src/controllers/v1/photographers/contactPhotographer.go — pass c.IP() through
  • cmd/api/main.go — start the ticker

Acceptance criteria

  • A valid inquiry returns 200 and writes a pending row; no email leaves immediately.
  • The email is delivered roughly 30 minutes later and the row flips to sent.
  • Exceeding the per-IP or per-email hourly limit writes a blocked row and sends nothing, while the response is unchanged.
  • The same message body submitted repeatedly scores as duplicate.
  • Blocked rows carry spam_score and spam_reasons so they can be reviewed.
  • Two API processes running at once never send the same inquiry twice.
  • Tests cover the scoring function and the claim query.

Open question

"IP reputation checks" in #101 means an external vendor (AbuseIPDB, IPQS) — a new dependency, ongoing cost, and latency on the request path. Everything else here works without it. Confirm whether that service is actually being purchased before wiring it in; if not, per-IP counters cover the same ground for phase one.

issues.main_description_html:
Implementation Record: Decoupled Timezone Validation and Spoken Language Catalog Seeding

Metadata

  • Issues:
    • #102 — Resolve Time Zone Validation Error on Directory Application Endpoint
    • #104 — Fix Invalid timezone and Invalid language rejections on apply and profile update
  • Pull Request: #106 — Enhance timezone and language validation across photographer application
  • Date: 2026-09-16
  • Status: Implemented & Verified

1. Problem & Root Cause Analysis

Timezone Rejections (#102 & #104)

The timezones database catalog table previously held only a single seeded row: America/Toronto (src/action/v1/photographers/migrateRoleProfile.go:187-195).

During photographer directory application (POST /v1/photographers/apply) and profile updates (PATCH /v1/photographers/:gothruUserId/profile), validation looked up exact matches against that table (src/helpers/photographerRole.go):

config.GetConnPhotographers().Table("timezones").Where("name = ?", name).Count(&count)
if count == 0 { return ErrInvalidTimezone }

Any applicant or photographer located outside Toronto submitting an authentic IANA timezone identifier (Asia/Jakarta, Europe/London, America/New_York, etc.) matched zero rows and was rejected with HTTP 400 Invalid timezone.

Furthermore, the backend exposed GET /v1/photographers/timezones, which returned only America/Toronto. In the dashboard frontend (gothru-dashboard src/pages/Photographer/hooks/usePhotographerCatalogs.jsx):

timezones: timezones?.length ? timezones : FALLBACK_TIMEZONES,

Because the endpoint succeeded and returned a 1-item array, timezones?.length evaluated to truthy. This collapsed the dropdown to a single option (America/Toronto) and blocked the browser's native Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone') fallback from ever running.

Language Rejections (#104)

The languages catalog table was previously seeded with only English. Validation checked comma-separated language strings against the table (ValidateLanguages). Choosing any other language offered by the frontend dropdown (such as French, Spanish, Indonesian) resulted in HTTP 400 Invalid language.

2. Architecture & Design Decisions

Standard Library Timezone Validation (time.LoadLocation)

Instead of maintaining an internal catalog table mirroring the world's timezones, timezone validation is now performed entirely in-memory using Go's standard library time.LoadLocation(name).

Mandatory Guards:

  1. Empty / Whitespace Guard: time.LoadLocation("") returns time.UTC with nil error in Go. Empty and whitespace-only inputs must be explicitly rejected.
  2. "Local" Guard: time.LoadLocation("Local") resolves to time.Local (the server's local clock). This is explicitly rejected so users must supply canonical IANA timezone names.
func ValidateTimezone(name string) error {
	if strings.TrimSpace(name) == "" || name == "Local" {
		return ErrInvalidTimezone
	}
	if _, err := time.LoadLocation(name); err != nil {
		return ErrInvalidTimezone
	}
	return nil
}

Binary-Embedded Timezone Database (time/tzdata)

Added import _ "time/tzdata" to cmd/api/main.go and test suites. This embeds the full IANA timezone database (~450KB) directly into the compiled Go binary, ensuring validation succeeds identically across minimal Docker containers (Alpine, scratch) and operating systems without relying on host system zoneinfo files.

Deletion of Stranded Timezones Catalog Endpoint & Table

Since backend validation no longer queries the timezones table, the GET /v1/photographers/timezones endpoint was advertising a single-row list that contradicted the validator.
Deleting the endpoint, its action, controller, model (DirectoryTimezone), and seed resolves the UI collapse:

  • The frontend's fetch to /photographers/timezones now triggers onError: () => setTimezones([]).
  • With timezones empty, usePhotographerCatalogs.jsx activates FALLBACK_TIMEZONES (Intl.supportedValuesOf?.('timeZone')).
  • The frontend dropdown natively exposes all ~400 browser IANA timezones, and every one of them passes backend validation.

Spoken Language Catalog Seeding (14 Languages)

Seeded the full set of 14 spoken languages offered by FALLBACK_LANGUAGES in gothru-dashboard:
English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Arabic, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Hindi, Russian, Indonesian.

Both the idempotent Go migration (MigrateRoleProfile) and the standalone SQL script (sql/2026-09-16-seed-languages.sql) are provided.

Bidirectional Automated Drift Prevention

To prevent drift between the Go migration slice and the manual SQL file, TestSeedLanguagesMatchesSQLFile parses the SQL file's VALUES clauses (ignoring comment lines) and asserts bidirectional equality (reflect.DeepEqual and map containment) against seedLanguages.

4. Deployment & Migration Instructions

  1. Timezone Validation:
    • No SQL migrations or database alterations required. Validation runs completely in-memory using the standard library.
  2. Language Seeding:
    Execute one of the following methods to populate the languages catalog table:
    • Method A (API Maintenance Endpoint):
      Call POST /v1/photographers/maintenance/migrate-role-profile.
    • Method B (Direct SQL Script):
      Execute sql/2026-09-16-seed-languages.sql on the photographers MySQL database: 
      mysql -u <user> -p photographers < sql/2026-09-16-seed-languages.sql
  3. Pre-Deploy Database Sanity Check:
    Before deploying to production, run the following query: 
    SELECT DISTINCT language FROM photographers;
    If any legacy rows contain languages outside the 14 seeded names (from older Node-era submissions), add those names to the languages table so those photographers can continue updating their profiles without validation rejection.

5. Verification

# Run unit and integration tests across affected packages

# Verify static analysis

# Verify compilation
go build ./...

All tests pass cleanly with 100% success rate and zero warnings.

Root cause and fix for #102.

Scope note: the languages catalog is broken in exactly the same way, in the same two call sites and the same two files. It is folded in here so one PR covers both — splitting it would mean two branches editing src/helpers/photographerRole.go and src/action/v1/photographers/migrateRoleProfile.go at the same time. Say so if you would rather track it separately.

Root cause

The timezones catalog table holds exactly one row, America/Toronto. That single INSERT at src/action/v1/photographers/migrateRoleProfile.go:187-195 is the only write to the table anywhere in the repo:

db.Model(&models.DirectoryTimezone{}).Where("name = ?", "America/Toronto").Count(&timezoneCount)
if timezoneCount == 0 {
    db.Create(&models.DirectoryTimezone{Name: "America/Toronto"})
}

Validation is an exact-match lookup against that table, src/helpers/photographerRole.go:112-120:

config.GetConnPhotographers().Table("timezones").Where("name = ?", name).Count(&count)
if count == 0 { return ErrInvalidTimezone }

ErrInvalidTimezone is errors.New("Invalid timezone") (src/helpers/photographerRole.go:20) — the exact warning in the report.

So any applicant outside Toronto submits a real IANA zone (Asia/Jakarta, Europe/London, …), matches zero rows, and is rejected. Applicants in Toronto pass, which is why this does not reproduce for everyone.

languages has the identical shape: seeded with only English (migrateRoleProfile.go:175-184), validated by exact match (photographerRole.go:133-145), returning Invalid language. Both validators run on apply and on profile update:

  • src/action/v1/photographers/applyPhotographer.go:84 and :87
  • src/action/v1/photographers/updatePhotographerProfile.go:174 and :177

Fix — timezone

The catalog table is re-implementing the IANA tz database. The standard library already has it, so drop the DB lookup:

func ValidateTimezone(name string) error {
	if name == "" || name == "Local" {
		return ErrInvalidTimezone
	}
	if _, err := time.LoadLocation(name); err != nil {
		return ErrInvalidTimezone
	}
	return nil
}

Add import _ "time/tzdata" to cmd/api/main.go so validation does not depend on the host having tzdata installed (adds roughly 450KB to the binary).

The two guards are required, not decoration: time.LoadLocation("") returns UTC with no error, and "Local" resolves to whatever the server is set to. Without them an empty timezone would silently validate.

After this the timezones table is no longer the source of truth for validity, so a stale catalog can never reject a valid zone again.

Fix — language

No standard library equivalent here, Go has no list of language names, so languages stays table-driven and simply needs seeding with the full set the product offers. See the open question below.

Files

  • src/helpers/photographerRole.go — ValidateTimezone uses time.LoadLocation
  • cmd/api/main.go — blank import _ "time/tzdata"
  • src/action/v1/photographers/migrateRoleProfile.go — seed the real language list
  • sql/<date>-seed-languages.sql — or seed by hand, matching the existing sql/ convention

Acceptance criteria

  • Applying with Asia/Jakarta, Europe/London or any other valid IANA zone succeeds.
  • Applying with a junk string such as Not/AZone still returns Invalid timezone.
  • An empty or missing timezone still returns Invalid timezone (regression guard — this is the case LoadLocation would otherwise let through).
  • The same four cases behave identically on PATCH /v1/photographers/:gothruUserId/profile.
  • Every language offered in the frontend dropdown passes validation.
  • Tests cover valid zone, junk zone, empty string and "Local".

Open questions

  1. Does the frontend build its timezone dropdown from GET /v1/photographers/timezones? If it does, the table still needs a full seed to populate the list, and the frontend can use the browser-native Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone') instead, which would let the catalog endpoint and table be deleted outright. If it auto-detects with Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone, the table is already dead weight. Worth one message to the frontend team before writing any seed.
  2. Which languages should the catalog contain? That is a product decision, not a technical one. Seed whatever the frontend dropdown already lists.

Metadata

  • Issues / Context: Fix avatar upload failure on PATCH /v1/photographers/:gothruUserId/profile (avatar_upload_failed / role must be one of photographer_360, image_processing)
  • Pull Request: #109 — fix(photographers): allow partial updates on profile patch for avatar upload

  • Base: development
  • Date: 2026-09-21
  • Status: Implemented & Reviewed

1. Problem & Root Cause Analysis

Avatar Upload Failure

When a photographer uploads a new avatar via the dashboard UI, the frontend flow (API-New UploadAvatarAction → ProfileService::uploadAvatar) uploads the asset and then issues a partial update request:

PATCH /v1/photographers/:gothruUserId/profile
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "avatar": "https://storage.googleapis.com/.../avatar.jpg"
}

Previously, this call was rejected with HTTP 400 (translated by the client/gateway to HTTP 409 conflict):

{
  "statusCode": 409,
  "data": {
    "messages": "role must be one of photographer_360, image_processing",
    "reason": "avatar_upload_failed"
  }
}

Root Cause

During the role-profile feature implementation (PR #70), Role, Timezone, Language (as string), and Services (as required slice) were made strictly required non-pointer fields on UpdateProfileRequest:

type UpdateProfileRequest struct {
    ...
    Role     string `json:"role"`
    Timezone string `json:"timezone"`
    Language string `json:"language"`
}

Because UpdatePhotographerProfile unconditionally validated:

if !helpers.IsValidRole(req.Role) {
    return nil, fmt.Errorf("role must be one of %s, %s", helpers.RolePhotographer360, helpers.RoleImageProcessing)
}

Any partial PATCH payload omitting role unmarshaled into req.Role = "", immediately failing role validation. Furthermore, if role were supplied, the request would subsequently fail on missing timezone, language, or services.

This violated standard HTTP PATCH partial-update semantics and completely broke single-field modifications, specifically the avatar upload workflow.

2. Architecture & Design Decisions

D1: Pointer Fields (*string) on UpdateProfileRequest

Role, Timezone, and Language are changed to *string pointers, harmonizing them with the other optional fields (Avatar *string, Fullname *string, Services *[]int, etc.):

  • nil indicates the field was omitted from the PATCH payload; the photographer's current stored database value is preserved.
  • Non-nil values indicate explicit updates and are validated against established domain rules (IsValidRole, ValidateTimezone, ValidateLanguages).

D2: Conditional Services and Role Change Validation

  • When req.Role is omitted, the effective role defaults to photographer.Role (the photographer's current role in the database).
  • An omitted role is never hard-defaulted to photographer_360. Hard-defaulting would corrupt image_processing photographers performing partial updates (e.g. uploading an avatar) by erroneously triggering a role change.
  • When req.Services is omitted (nil) and no role change occurs, existing services in photographers_services remain completely untouched.
  • If a client explicitly changes role (roleChanged := req.Role != nil && *req.Role != photographer.Role), services remain strictly required (services is required and must contain at least one service when changing role), and old role equipment is cleared in accordance with PRD specifications.

D3: Data Race & Goroutine Seam (afterProfileSave)

UpdatePhotographerProfile triggers background tasks (RecomputeAndSaveRanking and RevertApprovedToPendingOnSave) via goroutines upon save.

In unit tests with sqlmock (e.g., TestUpdatePhotographerProfile_AvatarOnly), these background goroutines outlive the test function. A deferred restoration of config.ConnPhotographers to origConn without lock synchronization caused a data race with background goroutines calling config.GetConnPhotographers() under read-lock.

To solve this cleanly:

  • Added a package-level function seam in updatePhotographerProfile.go: 
    var afterProfileSave = func(gothruUserId uint64) {
    go RecomputeAndSaveRanking(gothruUserId)
    go RevertApprovedToPendingOnSave(gothruUserId)
}
  • Unit tests that reach the end of UpdatePhotographerProfile stub afterProfileSave to a no-op: 
    origAfterSave := afterProfileSave
afterProfileSave = func(uint64) {}
defer func() {
    afterProfileSave = origAfterSave
}()
  • This eliminates goroutine leaks, data races, and the need for artificial nil guards in production database code.

Description

GET /v2/photographers/users returns 500 on page 2 and later whenever a continent, country or city filter is set:

GET /v2/photographers/users?size=12&countryId=233&role=photographer_360&cursor=61
→ 500 {"error":"Error 1052 (23000): Column 'id' in where clause is ambiguous"}

A location filter joins city, country and continent, and each of those tables has its own id column. The keyset cursor clause in src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers.go uses unqualified column names (id < ?, rating_avg, and the columns inside effectiveRankingExpr), so MySQL can't tell which id is meant. Without a location filter there is no join, which is why the global directory pages fine.

Impact on production: the frontend shows 0 results on page 2 of every country and city page. /virtual-tour-services-united-states has 30 photographers but only the first 12 can be reached.

  1. The cursor WHERE clause (and the ORDER BY it mirrors) qualifies every photographers column as photographers.<col>.
  2. No change to ordering, page size, or the response shape.

Acceptance criteria

  • ?countryId=233&role=photographer_360&size=12 walks 3 pages (12 + 12 + 6 = 30), with no 500 and no duplicate slugs.
  • The same walk works with continentId and with cityId.
  • The unfiltered walk returns the same order as before.

issues.main_description_html:
Description

The directory shows three different photographer counts for one country, and none of them matches the list. Example, United States (country 233):

Where Source Counts Value
Hero "Photographers" GET /v1/photographers/count map markers: status 3 with lat/lng, plus agency sublocations via UNION ALL (a photographer can count twice) 32
Country dropdown GET /v1/geodata/countries → GetBulkCountryPhotographerCounts distinct photographers, status 3, main location or any sublocation, every role 31
The list GET /v2/photographers/users status 3/4, role, main location only 30

/v2/photographers/users already returns a total, but it is len(result), the size of the current page, so the frontend cannot use it.

Requirements

Decision (2026-09-23): a photographer serves a place through its main city or any sublocation, the same rule #86 uses for active cities. The list follows the dropdowns, not the other way round.

  1. /v2/photographers/users location filters (continent, country, city) match a photographer through its main city or a sublocation. Each photographer is still one row.
  2. total is the number of rows the same query matches, before cursor and limit: the same status, role, location and search filters.
  3. The continent, country and city counts (GetBulk*PhotographerCounts, used by the geodata endpoints and search/location) count distinct photographers under the list's rules: status 3/4, role photographer_360, main city or sublocation.
  4. Caches written under the old rules are not served after deploy.
  5. /v1/photographers/count stays as is. It counts map markers, which is what the map needs.

Acceptance criteria

  • ?countryId=233&role=photographer_360 → total: 31 on every page, and walking every page yields exactly 31 photographers, including alin-bugeag-iki6 (main city outside the US, sublocation in the US).
  • For every continent, every country with photographers, and every US city, the dropdown count equals the list's total and the number of photographers walked.
  • #86 still holds: a city served only by a sublocation is listed and searchable.

Frontend follow-up: GoThruMedia/gothru-photographer-v2 uses this total for the hero and the results badge (GoThruMedia/gothru-photographer-v2#81).
